**他們的信心。**就是那四個抬癱子的人和癱子的信心。他們把房頂拆了一個洞，雄辯地證明他們迫切感到需要，以及他們只有耶穌表示滿意的信心。在耶穌對身體或心靈施展醫治之能以前，這種需求感和信心是很重要的（見路5:8註釋）。
**小子。**teknon，直譯是“孩子”。在它用於稱呼，像這裡那樣時，意思是“我的孩子”，“我的兒子”。他的疾病是他的生活不檢點的直接結果（《歷代願望》267頁），所以他的故事似乎很像那個浪子（見路15:13,14）幾個月前在畢士大醫好的癱子，情況顯然也是這樣（見約5:14）。
**你的罪赦了。**見10節註釋。痛苦給了他反省的時間。他認識到他的罪惡是造成他受苦的原因。耶穌所提到的，就是這些重重地壓在他心頭的罪惡。這個癱子來尋求的，既是身體的醫治，也是心靈的健康（見《歷代願望》267，268頁）。他在身體是無助的，在心靈是絕望的，直到他把自己的情況帶到能給他帶來幫助和希望的耶穌面前。見約9:2註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第125頁；《服務真詮》第174頁；《證言》卷六第232頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–11節）**。《證言》卷六第234頁。

10.en:
**That ye may know.** Jesus offered a miracle that all could see as evidence of the reality of a far greater miracle that they could not see (cf. Rom. 1:20).
**The Son of man.** Here, for the first time, all three synoptic writers use this distinctive title (Matt. 9:6; Mark 2:10; Luke 5:24). It was Christ’s favorite designation for Himself, and appears in the Gospels some 80 times. No one, however, addressed Him by this title, nor do any of the gospel writers refer to Him by it. This title was understood at least among some Jews as a name for the Messianic ruler of the new kingdom to be established. Except under oath (Matt. 26:63, 64; Mark 14:61, 62), and in private to those ready to believe in Him as the Christ (Matt. 16:16, 17; John 3:13–16; 4:25, 26; 16:30, 31), Jesus made no direct Messianic claims. It was His purpose that men should recognize in His life, His words, and His works, evidence that the prophecies of the Messiah had met their fulfillment in Him. See p. 209.
Jesus was literally “the Son of man,” both in a purely historic sense (see Luke 1:31–35; Rom. 1:3, 4; Gal. 4:4) and in a higher sense. The title, Son of man, designates Him as the incarnate Christ (see John 1:14; Phil. 2:6–8). It points to the miracle whereby Creator and creature were united in one divine-human person. It testifies to the truth that sons of men may indeed become sons of God (John 1:12; Gal. 4:3–7; 1 John 3:1, 2). Deity was identified with humanity in order that humanity might be made over again into the image of divinity (DA 25). Concerning Jesus as the Son of God, see on Luke 1:35; John 1:1–3; and as Son of man, on Luke 2:49, 52; John 1:14; see Additional Note on John 1.
**Power.** Gr. exousia, “authority.” The usual Greek word for “power,” in the sense of “might” or “strength,” is dunamis. To work a miracle required power, but the forgiveness of sin was a matter of authority. In the present passage, exousia stands at the beginning of the clause, and so emphasizes Christ’s authority to forgive sin. The Jewish leaders repeatedly challenged this authority (see ch. 11:28).
**Forgive sins.** The cause of the disease must be removed before the sufferer could be relieved of the disease from which he suffered (see on v. 5). Healing of the body without healing of the soul could result only in a repetition of the course the young man had taken that brought on the disease. Therefore Christ, who gave the man a new body, first provided him with a new heart.
**He saith.** The parenthetical statement introduced by these words is inserted in the middle of Jesus’ pronouncement to indicate that at this point He turned from the scribes and addressed Himself to the paralytic. It appears at the same place in all three accounts of the narrative (see Matt. 9:6; Luke 5:24). Similar examples of identical language may be found in Mark 1:16 and Matt. 4:18; Mark 5:28 and Matt. 9:21; Mark 14:2 and Matt. 26:5; Mark 15:10 and Matt. 27:18. See pp. 177, 178; cf. pp. 306, 307.
10.zh:
但要叫你們知道，人子在地上有赦罪的權柄。就對癱子說：

**但要叫你們知道。**耶穌行了一個神蹟，叫大家都把它看作一個大得多神蹟的證據（參羅1:20）。
**人子。**三位同觀福音的作者第一次在這裡使用了這個特殊稱號（太9:6；可2:10；路5:24）。基督很喜歡自稱為“人子”，在福音書中約出現80次。但沒有一個人用這個稱呼叫祂，也沒有一個福音書的作者用這個稱號稱祂。這個稱呼至少在一些猶太人中被理解為要建立之新國度的統治者彌賽亞的一個名號。基督除了宣誓承認（太26:63,64；可14:61,62）和私下對相信祂為基督的人（太16:16,17；約3:13-16；4:25,26；16:30,31）之外，沒有直接說自己是彌賽亞。祂的目的是要人們祂的生活、言語和工作中認出祂來，看明有關彌賽亞的預言已完全應驗在祂身上。見本卷註釋第209頁。
耶穌從純歷史的意義上（見路1:31-35；羅1:3,4；加4:4）和更高的意義上看，都確實是“人子”。“人子”的稱呼說明祂是成了肉身的基督（見約1:14；腓2:6-8）。它指出創造主和受造者在一位具有神人二性者身上結合的奇蹟。它證明人類確實可以變成上帝兒子的真理（約1:12；加4:3-7；約壹3:1,2）。神性與人性相結合，為了使人類可以恢復上帝的形象（《歷代願望》25頁）。關於耶穌作為上帝的兒子，見路1:35；約1:1-3；關於耶穌為人子，見路2:49,52；約1:14註釋；見《約翰福音》第1章補充註釋。
**赦罪。**在病人解除病痛之前，必須先消除病因（見第5節註釋）。光醫治身體而不醫治心靈，只能使這個青年人重蹈使他罹患疾病的覆轍。所以基督在給這個人新的身體之前，先給他一顆新心。
**權柄。**exousia，“權威”。希臘語表示“能力”用dunamis。行神蹟需要能力，赦免罪惡則需要權柄。在本段中exousia位於句首，強調基督赦罪的權柄。猶太領袖們多次質疑這個權柄（見可11:28）。
**就對癱子說。**這句話插在耶穌所說的話中，說明祂此刻轉離文士對癱子說話。在三部同觀福音的記錄中，它都出現在相同的位置（見太9:6；路5:24）。類似相同用語的例子可以在可1:16和太4:18；可5:28和9:21；可14:2和太26:5；可15:10和太27:18中找到。見本卷註釋第177,178頁；參第306,307頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第270頁。

6.en:
**The scribes.** See p. 55, and on ch. 1:22. According to Luke (see on ch. 5:17) these “Pharisees and doctors of the law” came from all parts of “Galilee, and Judaea, and Jerusalem.” The coming of representatives from so many different places suggests that their presence upon this particular occasion was more than casual. The fact that these religious officials were from precisely the areas in which Jesus thus far had worked would seem to indicate that they were at Capernaum to investigate the One who had become the center of such intense public interest. The situation recalls the delegation that the leaders in Jerusalem dispatched to the Jordan to investigate the work of John the Baptist (John 1:19–28) two years previously. The present delegation from Judea, where Jesus had previously worked, may have been summoned to advise the leaders in Galilee regarding their course of action in view of Jesus’ more recent activities there.
These men were spies (see DA 267; cf. 213), and as if to remind them vividly of the healing of the paralytic at Bethesda (John 5:1–9), Jesus now healed another man suffering from the same disease. They did not have long to wait before finding what they were looking for—alleged evidence that Jesus was a blasphemer. His earlier statement before the Jewish leaders had been branded blasphemy (John 5:18); now He exercised publicly a divine prerogative that they likewise took to be blasphemy. This incident marks the first of Jesus’ several controversies with the Jewish authorities during His Galilean ministry.
**Reasoning.** Gr. dialogizomai, “to balance accounts,” “to converse,” “to debate,” “to argue.”
6.zh:
有幾個文士坐在那裡，心裡議論，說：

**文士。**見本卷註釋第55頁，和可1:22註釋。路加說（見路5:17註釋），這些“法利賽人和教法師”是從“加利利各鄉村和猶太並耶路撒冷來的”。代表們來自這許多不同的地區，說明他們的到場並非偶然。這些宗教官員來自耶穌迄今工作過的地區，這表明他們在迦百農是要調查這已變成公眾強烈關注中心的人。這種情形使人想起兩年前耶路撒冷的領袖們曾派代表團去約旦河，調查施洗約翰的工作（約1:19-28）。鑑於耶穌最近在加利利的活動，這個來自猶大，就是耶穌先前工作過地方的代表團，可能被召來，就應該採取什麼行動方針，為加利利的領袖提供諮詢。
這些人是探子（見《歷代願望》207頁；參213頁）。，耶穌現在醫好了一個癱子，似乎清楚地使他們想起了祂曾在畢士大醫好了另一個癱子（約5:1-9）。他們沒有等多久就發現了他們正要找的所謂的證據——耶穌是一個褻瀆者。他先前在猶太領袖們面前所講的話曾被汙衊褻瀆（約5:18）；現在祂公開行使了一項神聖的特權，他們同樣稱之為褻瀆。這件事標誌著耶穌在加利利傳道期間與猶太當局的第一次論戰。
**議論。**Dialogizomai（“結帳”，“交談”，“爭論”）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷八第202頁。

27.en:
**Sabbath.** See on Gen. 2:1–3; Ex. 20:8–11.
**For.** Literally, “for the sake of.”
**Man.** Gr. anthrōpos, literally, “a person,” a generic term including men, women, and children (see on ch. 6:44). “Mankind” would reflect the meaning of anthrōpos more accurately. The Sabbath was designed and ordained by a loving Creator for the welfare of humanity. It is only by the wildest stretch of reasoning that a person could consider the Sabbath “against” man in any respect (see on Col. 2:14).
**Not man for the sabbath.** God did not create man because He had a Sabbath and needed someone to keep it. Rather, an Allwise Creator knew that man, the creature of His hand, needed opportunity for moral and spiritual growth, for character development. He needed time in which his own interests and pursuits should be subordinated to a study of the character and will of God as revealed in nature, and later, in revelation. The seventh-day Sabbath was ordained of God to meet this need. To tamper in any way with the Creator’s specifications as to when and how the day should be observed is tantamount to denying that God knows what is best for the creatures of His hand.
God ordained that the Sabbath should be a blessing, not a burden, and it is to man’s interest and not his injury to observe it. It was designed to increase his happiness, not to work a hardship on him. Sabbath-keeping does not consist essentially in the petty observance of certain formalities and in abstention from certain pursuits; to think of it in this light is to miss completely the true spirit and objectives of Sabbath observance and to engage in the pursuit of righteousness based on works. We refrain from certain tasks, from certain pursuits, from certain topics of thought and conversation, not because that by so doing we think to win favor with God. We refrain from these things in order that we may devote our time, our energies, and our thought to other pursuits that will increase our understanding of God, our appreciation of His goodness, our capacity to cooperate with Him, and our ability to serve Him and our fellow men more effectively. Sabbathkeeping that consists only, or primarily, in the negative aspect of not doing certain things is not Sabbathkeeping at all; it is only when the positive aspect of Sabbathkeeping is practiced that we may hope to derive from Sabbath observance the benefit ordained by a wise and loving Creator. See on Isa. 58:13.
The legion requirements of the rabbis pertaining to the meticulous observance of the Sabbath were based on the concept that the Sabbath was of more importance in the sight of God than man himself. According to the apparent reasoning of these blind exponents of the divine law, man was made for the Sabbath—made to keep it mechanically. The rabbis reduced the Sabbath to an absurdity by their rigid and meaningless distinction between what might and what might not be done on that day (see on v. 24). They emphasized the negative aspect of Sabbath observance—of refraining from certain things. The forms of religion were set forth as the substance of it.
27.zh:
又對他們說：安息日是為人設立的，人不是為安息日設立的。

**安息日。**見創2:1-3；出20:8-11註釋。
**為。**直譯是“為……的緣故”。
**人。**anthrōpos，泛指男人、女人和孩子（見可6:44註釋）。譯為“人類”更為準確。安息日是慈愛的創造主為人類的福利而設立的。只有最不合理的推論才會認為安息日在任何方面與人“有礙”（見西2:14註釋）。
**人不是為安息日設立的。**上帝造人並不是因為祂有一個安息日需要人遵守。而是全智的創造主知道祂手所造的人需要道德和屬靈成長以及品格發展的機會。人需要有時間把他的興趣和追求投入研究大自然和聖經所啟示的上帝旨意和祂的品格。第七日安息日是上帝所設立來滿足這個需要的。以任何方式篡改創造主關於何時並如何遵守這日的具體要求，就等於否認上帝知道什麼對祂手所造的生物是最好的。
上帝規定安息日應成為一個福氣，而不是一個重擔；遵守安息日帶給人的是益處而不是傷害。安息日的設立是要增進人的幸福，而不是要給人造成艱難困苦。守安息日主要不在於謹慎地遵從某些儀式，戒絕某些事務。以這種觀點考慮安息日就是完全沒有理解遵守安息日的真正精神和目標，而追求出於行為的義。我們不做某些工，不從事某些事，不思考也不談論某些話題，不是因為我們想要藉此獲得上帝的恩寵。我們不做這些事是為了將我們的時間，精力和思想專注於其他事務。這些事務可以增進我們對上帝的理解，對祂良善的感激和與祂合作的能力，並使我們更有效地服侍祂和我們的同胞。僅僅或者主要是在消極方面不做某些事，根本就不是守安息日；只有實行守安息日的積極方面，我們才有希望通過遵守安息日得到智慧慈愛的創造主所規定的益處。見賽58:13註釋。
與謹慎遵守安息日相關的大量拉比的要求，是基於在上帝看來安息日比人更重要的觀念。按照對上帝律法的盲目理解所得出的結論是：人是為安息日設立的，是為機械地遵守安息日而造的。拉比們通過嚴格地、無意義地區分在安息日可以做什麼不可以做什麼，使安息日成了一件荒唐事（見24註釋）。他們強調遵守安息日的消極方面，剋制不做某些事，把宗教的形式說成是宗教的實質。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第533頁；《證言》卷二第582頁；《證言》卷四第247頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（27–28節）**。《歷代願望》第285，288頁。

9.en: **Whether is it easier?** Apparently the scribes were thinking, “It is easy to say that a man’s sins are forgiven, for no one can really tell whether they are.” Jesus immediately took up their unspoken challenge and, in substance, inquired: “Which would you find easier, to forgive a man’s sins or to heal him of paralysis?” The answer was obvious.
9.zh:
或對癱子說你的罪赦了，或說起來！拿你的褥子行走；哪一樣容易呢？

哪一樣容易呢？文士們顯然認為：“說一個人的罪赦了要容易一些，因為誰也不知道有沒有赦免。”耶穌立即接受他們沒有說出來的挑戰，實際上是在問道：“赦免一個人的罪，或醫好癱瘓，你們認為哪一樣容易呢？”答案是顯而易見的。

7.en:
**This man.** Gr. houtos, “this [one],” as if spoken in contempt. They thought they had caught Jesus in the act of blasphemy, but strangely enough, the evidence was not such that they could bring it against Him at His trial a year and a half later (Matt. 26:59, 60; Mark 14:55, 56). Their difficulty lay in the fact that He confronted them with the practical operation of the power of Deity—in forgiving sin and healing disease—rather than the assertion of specific Messianic claims. See p. 209.
**Blasphemies.** Gr. blasphēmiai, “injurious speeches,” “slanders,” that is, any derogatory statements. The scribes assumed that in forgiving the paralytic’s sins Jesus, a mere man as they claimed, had usurped the prerogatives of Deity. Under the ceremonial system the priest presided over a man’s confession but did not actually speak words of forgiveness. His acceptance of the sacrifice merely symbolized God’s acceptance of the confession (see Heb. 10:1–12). By their refusal to recognize evidence of the presence and operation of divinity the scribes were committing the very sin of which, in their hearts, they accused Christ (see Matt. 12:22–32). The Levitical penalty for blasphemy was death by stoning (Lev. 24:16), although the Jews in Jesus’ time were not generally at liberty to carry it out.
**Who can forgive?** The scribes were strictly correct so far as their theology was concerned, for the OT clearly pointed to God as the One who forgives sin (Isa. 43:25; Jer. 31:34; cf. John 10:33). Their error was in failing to recognize that the Man who stood before them was God. See p. 209.
7.zh:
這個人為什麼這樣說呢？他說僭妄的話了。除了神以外，誰能赦罪呢？

**這個人。**houtos，帶著蔑視的語氣。他們以為自己已經抓住了耶穌褻瀆的把柄，但是非常奇怪，一年半以後祂受審時，他們沒有用這證據來指控祂（太26:59,60；可14:55,56）。他們的難處在於祂讓他們面對上帝能力實際的運行——赦免罪惡和醫治疾病——而沒有明確宣佈自己是彌賽亞。見本卷註釋第209頁。
**僭妄的話。**blasphēmiai，“有害的言論”，“誹謗”，即任何毀謗的言論。文士們認為耶穌如他們所說只是一個人，竟然赦免這癱子的罪，從而篡奪了上帝的權柄。在儀文制度下，祭司主持人的認罪，但實際上並不能說赦免的話。他接受獻祭只是象徵上帝接受認罪（見來10:1-12）。文士們既不肯接受上帝臨格和運行的證據，就犯了他們心中控告基督所犯的罪（見太12:22-32）。摩西的律法對褻瀆的刑罰是用石頭打死（利24:16），儘管耶穌時代的猶太人一般沒有權利執行這種刑罰。
誰能赦罪呢？根據他們的教義，文士們是絕對正確的，因為《舊約》清楚地指出只有上帝才能赦免罪惡（賽43:25；耶31:34；參約10:33）。他們錯在未能認出站在他們面前的就是上帝。見本卷註釋第209頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第269頁；《服務真詮》第76頁。

22.en:
**New wine.** See on Luke 5:39. By “new wine” is meant wine in which the forces of fermentation have not begun their work, or in which the work has been begun but not completed. The representation of the gospel by “new wine” and its work by the process of fermentation resembles in essence the parable of the leaven, but emphasizes a different result (see on Matt. 13:33). The “new wine” represents the vital truth of God at work in the hearts of men.
**Bottles.** In ancient times these would be wineskins, which were skins of sheep or goats with the skin of the legs sewn up, and the neck serving as a mouth of the bottle. “Old bottles” would have lost their original resilience, and become dry and hard. Such was the condition of Judaism in the time of Christ.
**Burst the bottles.** Jesus’ revolutionary teachings could not be reconciled with the reactionary dogmas of Judaism. Any effort to contain Christianity within the dead forms of Judaism, that is, to unite the two by forcing Christianity to take the shape of, and be reconciled to it, would prove vain. Jesus taught that the principles of the kingdom of heaven applied to the souls of men would lead to the outworking of those principles in lives of active, radiant religion (see on Matt 5:2).
**Wine is spilled.** The attempt to unite the new with the old would result in two-fold destruction. The “wine” of the gospel would be “spilled,” and the “bottles” of Judaism would be “marred.”
**New bottles.** Probably either a reference to the people ready to receive the gospel or to the new type of church organization through which the gospel was to be promoted.
22.zh:
也沒有人把新酒裝在舊皮袋裡，恐怕酒把皮袋裂開，酒和皮袋就都壞了；惟把新酒裝在新皮袋裡。

**新酒。**見路5:39註釋。“新酒”指還沒有發酵的，或已開始發酵卻還沒有發成的。“新酒”代表福音；發酵的過程代表福音的工作，與面酵的比喻相似，但強調不同的結果（見太13:33註釋）。“新酒”代表上帝充滿生命力的真理在人心中的工作。
**皮袋。**古時指葡萄酒囊，用綿羊或山羊皮製成的，腳部的皮縫起來，頸部作為瓶口。“舊皮袋”會失去其原有的彈性，變得又乾又硬。基督時代猶太教的狀況就是這樣。
**把皮袋裂開。**耶穌的革命性教訓與猶太教的反動教條格格不入。把基督教包括在猶太教僵死的形式中，即通過強迫基督教接受猶太教的形式並與之協調而使兩者結合起來的努力必是徒然的。耶穌教導說，天國的原則應用於人們的心靈，會在他們積極發光的宗教生活中實行出來（見太5:2註釋）。
**酒…壞了。**把新與舊放在一起，會使兩者都毀壞。福音的“酒”會“灑了”；猶太教的“皮袋”會“壞了”。
**新皮袋。**可能要麼是指準備接受福音的人，要麼是指藉以傳揚福音的新型教會組織。
[在安息日掐麥穗：可2:23-28=太12:1-8=路6:1-5。註釋主要在《馬可福音》。見本卷註釋218頁地圖] 。
**懷愛倫註釋**。見太9：17懷愛倫註釋。

28.en:
**Therefore.** After pointing to the purpose of the Sabbath (v. 27) Christ directs attention to its Author, and thus to His own right to determine how that purpose shall best be realized.
**Son of man.** See on Matt. 1:1; Mark 2:20; see Additional Note on John 1.
**Lord.** The Saviour Himself has the right to determine what is appropriate to that day; consequently, the Pharisees were exceeding their prerogatives (see v. 24). The church has no right to load the Sabbath with oppressive restrictions—as did the Jews—or to attempt the transfer of its sacredness from one day to another. Both are devices of the evil one designed to lure men away from the true spirit of Sabbath observance. Man has no right to tamper with the day of God’s choosing, whether he be Pharisee or Christian ecclesiastic.
**Also.** Or, “even.” The complete line of reasoning Christ set before the caviling Pharisees is more clearly presented in the account given by Matthew, as follows: (1) Human need is of more importance than ritual requirements or human traditions (see Matt. 12:3, 4). (2) The labor performed in connection with the Temple service is in keeping with the requirements of the Sabbath day (see v. 5). (3) Christ is greater than either the Temple (see v. 6) or the Sabbath day (see v. 8).
28.zh:
所以，人子也是安息日的主。

**所以。**基督在指出安息日的宗旨之後（27節），把人們的注意力指向安息日的設立者，從而說明祂自己有權決定如何最好地實現安息日的宗旨。
**人子。**見太1:1；可2:20註釋；見《約翰福音》第一章補充註釋。
**也是。**馬太的記錄更清楚地呈現了基督擺在吹毛求疵的法利賽人面前的完整的思路，例如：（1）人的需要比儀式的要求或人的傳統更加重要（見太12:3,4）。（2）與聖殿的崇祀有關的工作符合安息日的要求（見5節）。（3）基督比殿（見6節）或安息日（見8節）更大。
**主。**救主自己有權決定在那日做什麼是合適的；所以法利賽人越權了（見24節）。教會無權給安息日加上強迫性限制，像猶太人所做的那樣，或者企圖將其神聖性從一天轉移到另一天。這兩種做法都是那惡者所設計，引誘人離開遵守安息日的真精神。人沒有權利篡改上帝所選擇的日子，無論是法利賽人，還是基督教的教牧人員。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第447頁。

8.en: **Perceived.** Gr. epiginoskō, “to know accurately,” “to recognize.” Repeatedly Jesus read men’s thoughts (Mark 12:15; Luke 6:8; 9:47; 11:17; cf. John 4:16–19; 8:7–9). This generally had the effect of making them furiously angry.
8.zh:
耶穌心中知道他們心裡這樣議論，就說：你們心裡為什麼這樣議論呢？

**知道。**epiginoskō，“準確瞭解”，“認出”。耶穌一再看透人的心思（可12:15；路6:8；9:47；11:17；參約4:16-19；8:7-9）。這通常會惹怒他們。

1.zh:
過了些日子，耶穌又進了迦百農。人聽見他在房子裡，

**過了些日子。**di' hēmerōn。有人認為這是指耶穌第一次加利利之行的整段時間，從祂離開迦百農（可1:35-38）到祂回到該城。但這次旅行可能要延續好幾個星期，所以把這段“日子”理解為耶穌退到曠野的日子更加合適。那時因為人多，祂“不得再明明地進城”（可1:45）。這樣理解的話，這段時間就是指第1章結尾的事件和第2章開頭的事件之間了。
**耶穌又進了。**或“祂回到”。馬可用希臘詞palin（“再次”），主要表示祂以前提到的地方或相似的環境（見可2:13；3:1,20；4:1；5:21；8:13）。相比之下，馬太通常用palin開始新的敘述。馬太和馬可都注意到耶穌最近從祂第一次周遊加利利城鎮鄉村回來（見太9:1）。馬太補充說基督是坐船回迦百農的。祂的第一次旅行顯然結束於加利利湖東岸，或退到那個地區，因為那個醫好的麻風病人把祂傳開了；祂只好暫時脫離公開的傳道（見可1:45註釋）。
**迦百農。**見太4:13註釋。馬太稱迦百農為基督“自己的城”，即祂在加利利傳道的總部；祂似乎把迦百農看作自己的家。
**人聽見。**或“人們得知”。
**祂在房子裡。**原文暗示“祂在房子裡”直接引自人們的傳聞。只有馬可特別提到了這件事。他還提到了其他同觀福音的作者所省略的許多細節。“在房子裡”相當於“在家裡”，無疑指彼得的家（見《歷代願望》267頁；見可1:29註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–12節）**。《歷代願望》第262-271頁。
1.en:
**Again he entered.** [The Paralytic Lowered Through the Roof, Mark 2:1–12=Matt. 9:2–8=Luke 5:17–26. Major comment: Mark. See Early Galilean Ministry; The Ministry of Our Lord; on miracles pp. 208–213.] Or, “he returned” (RSV). Mark characteristically uses the Greek word palin, “again,” in referring to places he has mentioned previously, or to similar circumstances (see chs. 2:13; 3:1, 20; 4:1; 5:21; 8:13). By way of contrast, Matthew commonly uses palin to introduce a new section of his narrative. Both Matthew and Mark note the fact that Jesus had recently returned from His first tour through the towns and villages of Galilee (see Matt. 9:1). Matthew adds the information that Christ’s return to Capernaum was by boat. Evidently either His first tour ended on the eastern shore of the Lake of Galilee, or He had retired to that region when the publicity given Him by the healed leper led to a temporary withdrawal from public ministry (see on Mark 1:45).
**Capernaum.** See on Matt. 4:13. Matthew refers to Capernaum as Christ’s “own city”; that is, the headquarters from which He conducted His Galilean ministry and which He seems to have considered His home.
**After some days.** Gr. di’ hēmerōn, “after days.” This phrase is taken by some to refer to the whole period of Jesus’ First Galilean Tour, between the time of His departure from Capernaum (ch. 1:35–38) and His return to that city. Inasmuch, however, as that tour probably extended over a number of weeks, it may be more appropriate to understand the “days” here as being those during which Jesus retreated into the desert because of the crowds, when He “could no longer openly enter a town” (ch. 1:45, RSV). Thus understood, the period in question would be that between the events narrated at the end of ch. 1 and those at the beginning of ch. 2.
**It was noised.** Literally, “It was heard.”
**That.** Gr. hoti, “that,” which implies that the following words, literally, “he is in the house,” are a direct quotation of what was being reported by people generally.
**In the house.** Only Mark specifically mentions this fact, as is true of numerous details of the narrative that the other synoptists omit. This was equivalent to saying “at home,” a reference without doubt to the home of Peter (see DA 267, 271; see on ch. 1:29).

2.zh:
就有許多人聚集，甚至連門前都沒有空地；耶穌就對他們講道。

基督離開迦百農進行祂第一次傳道旅行，是因為公眾的興奮和大批群眾來尋祂（見可1:33,37）。但是祂離開迦百農並沒有使百姓的熱情減退。他們一知道耶穌回到了城裡，就朝祂蜂擁而來。
2.en: **Straightway.** Christ’s departure from Capernaum for His first missionary tour was occasioned by the popular excitement and the great throngs of people who came seeking Him (see ch. 1:33, 37). But His absence from Capernaum left the enthusiasm of the people unabated. No sooner was it known that Jesus was again in the city than the people flocked to Him.

3.zh:
有人帶著一個癱子來見耶穌，是用四個人抬來的；

**一個癱子。**paralutikos，“一個癱瘓病人”。
**四個人抬。**只有馬可提到這個細節。這個細節和其他細節不僅反映記錄的真實性，而且表明是出自目擊者，這次很可能是彼得（見本卷註釋第563頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–5節）**。《證言》卷三第168頁。
3.en:
**One sick of the palsy.** Gr. paralutikos, “a paralytic.”
**Borne of four.** A detail given by Mark only. This and other details not only reflect the factual nature of the account but also mark it as the account of an eyewitness, in this case probably Peter (see p. 563).

4.zh:
因為人多，不得近前，就把耶穌所在的房子，拆了房頂，既拆通了，就把癱子連所躺臥的褥子都縋下來。

**人多。**就是大批的人。
**拆了房頂。**路加（路5:19）說他們“從瓦間把他縋入”。這座房子象中東地區常見的房屋一樣，無疑有一個平頂，外面有樓道或梯子，可以從下面的院子上來（見徒10:9；參申22:8註釋）。屋頂顯然用瓦鋪在椽子上。
這種接近耶穌的特殊辦法，是那個癱子本人竭力提議的。他現在雖然離耶穌很近，還是擔心會喪失機會（見《歷代願望》268頁）。耶穌出人意外地離開迦百農（可1:37,38），好幾個星期都不在，最後又退到曠野裡（可1:45），這一切可能使這個面對夭折前景的人更加絕望了（見《歷代願望》267頁）。
**褥子。**krabbatos，窮人的“床”。這個人所躺臥的簡陋小床可能只是一個草蓆或褥子。
4.en:
**The press.** That is, the throng of people.
**Uncovered the roof.** Literally, “unroofed the roof.” Luke (ch. 5:19) records that they “let him down through the tiling.” As is common in the Middle East, this house doubtless had a flat roof, with a stairway or ladder on the outside which gave access to it from the courtyard below (see Acts 10:9; cf. on Deut. 22:8). Apparently the roof was made by laying tiles over the rafters.
This unusual method of reaching Jesus was the desperate suggestion of the paralytic himself, who feared that, though now so close to Jesus, he might yet lose his opportunity (see DA 268). The way in which Jesus had left Capernaum so unexpectedly (ch. 1:37, 38), had remained away for several weeks, and finally had secluded Himself in the desert (ch. 1:45), probably added to the desperation of this man, who faced the prospect of an early death (see DA 267).
**Bed.** Gr. krabbatos, a poor man’s “couch,” or “bed.” The rude pallet on which the man lay was probably little more than a grass mat or a padded quilt.

12.zh:
那人就起來，立刻拿著褥子，當眾人面前出去了，以致眾人都驚奇，歸榮耀與神，說：我們從來沒有見過這樣的事！

這個曾懷著深切的需要來到耶穌面前的人，帶著勝利的喜樂走了；而那些懷著自滿、驕傲和惡意來到祂面前的人，卻“驚異得啞口無言，徹底失敗”地離開了（《歷代願望》270頁）。人接近耶穌的精神，決定他們在祂裡面發現的是通往天國的踏腳石，還是導致滅亡的絆腳石（見太21:44；路2:34；彼前2:8）。
[呼召利未馬太：可2:13,14=太9:9=路5:27,28。註釋主要在《馬可福音》。見本卷註釋218頁地圖；231頁圖表]。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第269頁；《服務真詮》第77頁。
12.en: **On this fashion.** Or, “anything like this.” The man who had come into the presence of Jesus with a profound sense of need went away in triumphant joy, while those who came in self-satisfaction, pride, and malice went away “dumb with amazement and overwhelmed with defeat” (DA 270). The spirit in which men approach Jesus determines whether they find in Him a steppingstone to heaven or a stumbling block to destruction (see Matt. 21:44; Luke 2:34; 1 Peter 2:8).

13.zh:
耶穌又出到海邊去，眾人都就了他來，他便教訓他們。

這顯然只是迦百農一帶的短途旅行，不是加利利的主要佈道旅行。設立十二使徒和登山寶訓之後的第二次這樣的旅行，是在稍後才開始的。
13.en: **He went forth again.** [Call of Levi Matthew, Mark 2:13, 14=Matt. 9:9=Luke 5:27, 28. Major comment: Mark. See Early Galilean Ministry; The Ministry of Our Lord.] Apparently this was but a short journey in the vicinity of Capernaum, and not a major preaching tour of Galilee. The second such tour, which was preceded by the appointment of the Twelve and the Sermon on the Mount, did not begin until somewhat later.

14.zh:
耶穌經過的時候，看見亞勒腓的兒子利未坐在稅關上，就對他說：你跟從我來。他就起來，跟從了耶穌。

**看見。**見路5:27註釋。
**亞勒腓的兒子。**有人認為“亞勒腓的兒子利未”就是“亞勒腓的兒子雅各”（可3:18）。但鑑於上面有關利未就是馬太的證據，利未和雅各似乎肯定不是同一個人。無法確定他們是不是兄弟（見可3:18註釋）。
**利未。**路加也用“利未”的名字（路5:27），但馬太在同一故事中更喜歡用“馬太”的名字（太9:9）。馬太被稱為“稅吏”（太10:3），以及其他福音書在十二使徒名單中有馬太而沒有利未（可3:18；路6:15；參徒1:13），進一步說明這兩個名字是指同一個人。猶太人有一個以上的名字很普遍，如西門彼得和約翰馬可。見可3:14註釋。
**稅關。**就是稅務所，顯然在“海邊”（13節），可能是希律安提帕向經過大路的商隊和旅客收稅的一個辦事處。這條大路從大馬士革和東方，通往地中海（見賽9:1註釋）的多利買（亞柯），或從希律腓利的領土經過加利利湖。關於迦百農的戰略和商業地位，見太4:13和路4:31註釋。
在一般人看來，稅吏的聲名很不好。他們不僅常作羅馬壓迫的工具，而且往往為自己的利益敲詐勒索，利用職權壓迫並欺詐百姓。他們被所有的人所憎恨和輕視，為社會和宗教所拋棄。見本卷註釋第66頁；見路3:12註釋。
**你跟從我來。**這是基督邀請人作祂門徒的常用語（見太4:19；約1:43）。馬太已經準備好了在片刻之間蒙召作出自己一生的重大決定；其先決條件是他以前與耶穌的接觸。他心裡肯定早就想跟從祂了。但是因為他很清楚拉比們對稅吏的態度，所以就以為這位大拉比肯定不會屈尊收他作門徒。路加（路5:28）補充說，馬太為了跟從耶穌“撇下了所有的”。他撇下了有利可圖的工作去做沒有報酬的服務。
[馬太的筵席：可2:15-17=太9:10-13=路5:29-32。註釋主要在《馬可福音》。見本卷註釋219頁地圖；231頁圖表]。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。見路15：29懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–22節）**。《歷代願望》第272-280頁。
14.en:
**He saw.** See on Luke 5:27.
**Levi.** Luke also uses this name (ch. 5:27), but Matthew in the same story prefers the name Matthew (ch. 9:9). That the two names refer to the same man is indicated further by the fact that Matthew also is called “the publican [taxgatherer]” (ch. 10:3), and by the fact that in their lists of the Twelve, the other Gospels have Matthew and not Levi (Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15; cf. Acts 1:13). It was common for Jews to have more than one name, as Simon Peter and John Mark. See on Mark 3:14.
**The son of Alphæus.** Some have thought to identify “Levi the son of Alphaeus” with “James the son of Alphaeus” (ch. 3:18). However, in view of the evidence given above for the identity of Levi with Matthew, it appears certain that Levi and James were different men; whether they were brothers it is impossible to say (see on ch. 3:18).
**The receipt of custom.** That is, the tax office. It apparently was “by the sea side” (v. 13), and was probably an office at which Herod Antipas collected revenue from caravans and travelers passing along the main highway from Damascus and the East to Ptolemais (Accho) on the Mediterranean (see on Isa. 9:1), or over the Lake of Galilee from the territory of Herod Philip. As to the strategic, commercial location of Capernaum see on Matt. 4:13 and Luke 4:31.
In popular opinion tax collectors were considered disreputable. Not only were they frequently agents of Roman oppression, they also were often extortioners on their own account, who made use of their official power to oppress and defraud the people. They were hated and despised by all, as social and religious outcasts. See p. 66; see on Luke 3:12.
**Follow me.** The usual language Christ used in extending His invitation to discipleship (see Matt. 4:19; John 1:43). Called upon to make the great decision of his life on a moment’s notice, Matthew was ready; such a decision would presuppose his having had previous contact with Jesus. In his heart there must have been already a longing to follow Him. But since he knew full well the attitude of the rabbis toward tax collectors, it doubtless did not occur to him that this great Rabbi would condescend to have him among His disciples. Luke (ch. 5:28) adds that Matthew “left all” in order to follow Jesus; he left a profitable business to serve without pay.

15.zh:
耶穌在利未家裡坐席的時候，有好些稅吏和罪人與耶穌並門徒一同坐席；因為這樣的人多，他們也跟隨耶穌。

**坐。**katakeimai，“躺下。”雖然在舊約時代猶太人習慣坐著吃飯，但到了耶穌的時代，至少在一些比較前衛的人家裡，人們一般躺在餐桌旁的臥榻或睡椅上吃飯。他們靠在墊子上用左臂支撐自己。桌子的三面通常備有這種傾斜的臥榻，第四面留下供侍者上菜。馬太家備有這種餐桌，暗示他是一個富裕而有文化的人。
馬太家的筵席顯然發生在他蒙召以後幾個星期，也許是幾個月（見《歷代願望》342頁；見可5:21註釋）。插在這裡可能是為了完整地記錄馬太的經歷。
**席。**或“在桌旁”。該詞是譯者加上去的，為了完善上下文中所暗示的觀念（見第16節）。
**在他家裡。**根據上下文，顯然是在馬太家裡，耶穌被當作貴賓（又見路5:29；參《歷代願望》274頁）。
**稅吏。**telōnai，“收稅員”，（見可2:14；路3:12註釋）。
**罪人。**見第17節註釋。這種接觸當時似乎沒有結果，但後來無疑有收成。當五旬節聖靈沛降在信徒們上時，他們與跟從耶穌的人站在一起，成了真理的見證人（見《歷代願望》274，275頁）。
**他們。**就是接受祂教訓的人。一些人現在和馬太一樣，顯然支持耶穌了；還有一些人後來無疑這麼做了，特別是在耶穌復活以後（見《歷代願望》275頁）。
15.en:
**Sat.** [Matthew’s Feast, Mark 2:15–17=Matt. 9:10–13=Luke 5:29–32. Major comment: Mark. See Middle Galilean Ministry; The Ministry of Our Lord.] Gr. katakeimai, “to lie down.” Although in OT times it was usually the Jewish custom to sit while eating, by the time of Jesus, in the more pretentious houses at least, people commonly lay down to eat on a low platform or couch sloping away from the table. They rested on cushions and supported themselves by their left arms. The usual table was equipped on three sides with such slanting platforms, the fourth side being left open for attendants to serve the food. That Matthew’s home was equipped with such a table suggests that he was a man of means and culture.
Evidently the feast in Matthew’s home took place some weeks, perhaps months, after his call (see DA 342; see on ch. 5:21). It is recorded here probably in order to complete, in one context, the account of Matthew’s experiences.
**At meat.** Or, “at table” (RSV). This expression has been supplied by the translators to complete the idea implicit in the context (see v. 16).
**In his house.** The context makes apparent that this was Matthew’s house, and that Jesus was the guest of honor (see also Luke 5:29; cf. DA 274).
**Publicans.** Gr. telōnai, “tax collectors,” “revenue agents” (see on Mark 2:14; Luke 3:12).
**Sinners.** See on v. 17. Such contacts as this, seeming at the time fruitless perhaps, doubtless contributed to producing the harvest of those who took their stand with the followers of Jesus, and became witnesses to the truth, when the Spirit was poured out upon the believers at Pentecost (see DA 274, 275).
**They.** That is, those who accepted His teachings. Some in addition to Matthew apparently took their stand for Jesus now; others doubtless did so later, particularly after the resurrection (see DA 275).

16.zh:
法利賽人中的文士（有古卷：文士和法利賽人）看見耶穌和罪人並稅吏一同吃飯，就對他門徒說：他和稅吏並罪人一同吃喝嗎？

**法利賽人中的文士。**這些文士是法利賽人；有些文士是撒都該人，但大部分文士是法利賽人。他們對律法的細節特別關心（見第51,52,55頁）。我們可以視他們為“法利賽派的文士”，而不是“撒都該派的文士”。有文本為“文士和法利賽人”。
**門徒。**mathētai，“學生”，在福音書中通常指耶穌在傳道時陪伴祂幫助祂的那一群人。門徒是mathētai；基督是他們的didaskalos，（夫子”或“老師”，見約3:2註釋）。
文士們希望藉著向門徒抱怨，破壞他們對夫子的尊敬。路加說文士向門徒“發怨言”（路5:30），顯然是意識到直接攻擊耶穌對他們不起任何作用，正如先前制止祂的努力已證明無效一樣（見可2:6-11；約2:18-20；5:16-47）。
**吃喝。**與外邦人一起吃喝是違反儀文律法的，涉及儀文上的不潔淨（徒11:3）。實際上稅吏是歸如入外邦人一類的，所以被視為社會所拋棄的人（見可2:14；路3:12,13）。
16.en:
**Scribes and Pharisees.** Important textual evidence (cf. p. 146) may also be cited for the reading, “scribes of the Pharisees,” that is, scribes who were Pharisees. While some of the scribes were Sadducees, most were Pharisees, for it was the latter who took a particular interest in the minutiae of the law (see pp. 51, 52, 55). We may think of them as “Pharisee scribes” rather than “Sadducee scribes.”
**Disciples.** Gr. mathētai, “learners,” “pupils.” In the Gospels this word is generally used of the group that accompanied Jesus and assisted Him in His ministry. The disciples were mathētai; Christ was their didaskalos, “master” or “teacher” (see on John 3:2).
By complaining to the disciples, the scribes hoped to alienate their respect for their Master. Luke says that the scribes “murmured” against the disciples (Luke 5:30), apparently realizing that a direct attack on Jesus would avail them nothing, even as previous attempts to silence Him had proved fruitless (see Mark 2:6–11; John 2:18–20; 5:16–47).
**Eateth and drinketh.** To eat and drink with Gentiles was an infraction of the ritual law and involved ceremonial uncleanness (Acts 11:3). For practical purposes, tax collectors were classed with the Gentiles and thus were considered among the social outcasts (see on Mark 2:14; Luke 3:12, 13).

17.zh:
耶穌聽見，就對他們說：康健的人用不著醫生，有病的人才用得著。我來本不是召義人，乃是召罪人。

**康健的人。**hoi ischuontes，“有力量的人”。路加用的是hoi hugiainontes，“健全的人”。路加的用詞比較準確，源於一個常用的希臘詞語hugiēs，表示“健康”。保羅像路加一樣多次使用這個詞，表示“正”道（提前1:10），“純正的”話語（提後1:13）和在真道上“純全”（多1:13）。
**我來本不是。**基督在講述祂到地上使命的深奧真理時，揭露了法利賽人及其對基督與稅吏交往之態度的偽善和錯謬。如果這些人如法利賽人所聲稱的是罪人，他們就必定比別人有更大的需要。他們不正是基督要付出最大努力的對象嗎？祂已經來了，要“救”人（太1:21），但祂如果只能救準備好了的義人，就不可能是一位真正的救主。祂作為人類救主使命的試驗在於祂為罪人所能做的事情。
**義人。**法利賽人聲稱能藉著嚴格順從儀文律法的要求獲得義。後來耶穌說明這種“義”是假冒的，在祂來要宣佈的國度裡沒有任何價值（太5:20；參可23:1-33）。但這次為了辯論的緣故，祂假定認可他們暗示自己所擁有的個人之義（可2:16,17），藉此說明自己照顧稅吏們屬靈需要的理由。
實際上法利賽人經常犯他們所深惡痛絕之稅吏們的罪行。耶穌說他們“侵吞寡婦的家產”（太23:14），為了肥己而使貪財的兒子免於照顧上了年紀的父母（見可7:11註釋）。法利賽人就這樣強調法律上的正確性，卻往往假冒為善。另一方面，稅吏們並沒有假裝尊敬儀文，有時倒更能接受耶穌的教訓，儘管他們有罪。見路18:9-14註釋。
[關於禁食問題：可2:18-22=太9:14-17=路5:33-39。註釋主要在《馬可福音》。見本卷註釋219頁地圖；關於比喻見本卷註釋第203-207頁]。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第58頁；《基督教育原理》第252頁；《給傳道人的證言》第230，351頁；《證言》卷二第74頁；《證言》卷三第49頁；《證言》卷四第42頁；《證言》卷五第219頁；見太9：12，13懷愛倫註釋。
17.en:
**They that are whole.** Gr. hoi ischuontes, “those having strength.” Luke reads, hoi hugiainontes, “those who are sound.” Luke’s expression is a more exact term, from hugiēs, a usual Greek word for “health.” Paul repeatedly uses the same word as does Luke, and applies it to “sound” doctrine (1 Tim. 1:10), “sound” words (2 Tim. 1:13), and of being “sound” in the faith (Titus 1:13).
**I came not.** In stating the profound truth of the purpose of His mission to earth Christ revealed the hypocrisy and fallacy of the Pharisees and their attitude toward Christ’s association with tax collectors. If these men were such sinners as the Pharisees claimed, they must be in greater need than other men. Were they not then the very ones for whom Christ should put forth His best efforts? He had come to “save” men (Matt. 1:21), but if He were able only to save those who were already righteous, He could not be truly a Saviour. The test of His mission as the Saviour of men turned on the point of what He could do for sinners.
**The righteous.** The Pharisees claimed to be able to attain righteousness through strict compliance with the requirements of the ritual law. Later, Jesus made it clear that such “righteousness” was counterfeit and without value in the kingdom He had come to proclaim (Matt. 5:20; cf. ch. 23:1–33). But on this occasion, for the sake of argument, He granted their implied claim to personal righteousness (Mark 2:16, 17), for by so doing He was able to make clear the reason why He ought to minister to the spiritual needs of the publicans.
In actual fact, the Pharisees were at times guilty of the very sins they so bitterly detested in the tax collectors. Jesus declared that they would “devour widows’ houses” (Matt. 23:14) and release an avaricious son from caring for aged parents (see on Mark 7:11), if thereby they themselves might be enriched. Thus the Pharisees, laying emphasis on legal correctness, too often were hypocrites. On the other hand, the publicans, who made no pretense at ritualistic respectability, were sometimes in a better position to accept the teaching of Jesus, in spite of their sins. See on Luke 18:9–14.

18.zh:
當下，約翰的門徒和法利賽人禁食。他們來問耶穌說：約翰的門徒和法利賽人的門徒禁食，你的門徒倒不禁食，這是為什麼呢？

**約翰的門徒和法利賽人禁食。**也許譯成“正在禁食”更好。約翰的門徒在這裡的禁食表明，他們無疑至少在一定程度上採用了約翰節制的生活方式（見太3:4）。顯然，他們在向耶穌提出這個問題時，似乎確實正在禁食。
公元1世紀一份關於禁食的古猶太文獻Megillath Ta`anith，提到當時的猶太人一般在每週的第二日和第五日，即星期一和星期四禁食（見路18:12）。雖然猶太的傳統說法將這個習慣諸於摩西在西奈山40天禁食（見出34:28）從星期四開始，到星期一結束的傳說，但是將這兩日定為禁食的日子，是要讓它們離安息日遠一些，同時彼此又不靠得太近。見斯特拉克和比勒貝克《新約註釋》，卷二，第241-243頁。
古猶太教的主要權威斯特拉克和比勒貝克指出，一週兩次禁食的確切目的並不完全清楚，但它們似乎可能出於特別熱心的人設法挽回民族世俗化的願望。他們認為這種世俗化正迅速導致了民族的毀滅。一般說來，在古代猶太人中，個人的禁食是為了彌補一次罪行，或保證祈禱得到有利的應允，或完成一個願望。許多人禁食似乎確實是因為他們相信這種行為會在上帝面前為自己賺得特別的功勞。
禁食的這些用法當然是出於對上帝的品格和公義性質的誤解。禁食往往蛻變為靠行為稱義的一種手段；人們藉以盼望平息一位嚴酷上帝的怒氣並賺得祂的恩寵，而不管他們心靈的狀況。在耶穌時代之前的幾個世紀，眾先知曾斥責過這種觀念，宣稱上帝厭惡以色列人的禁食和其它宗教禮節（賽58:3-5；亞7:5,6）。
基督徒有時候需要敏銳的思想和有洞察力的判斷；他可能有重要的決定要做，或者可能需要更清楚地洞悉上帝的旨意。在這種情況下，禁食會證明是一種極大的福氣。這種禁食不一定意味著徹底禁絕食物，而是僅限於維持健康與生命的簡單必需飲食。基督徒可以像但以理一樣，禁除“美味”（但10:3）。任何削弱身體或損害健康的行為都不能榮耀上帝，也不能促進一個人的基督徒經驗。見太6:16。
**他們來問。**這裡沒有說明“他們”指誰，路加在這方面也沒有講清楚（見路5:33）。但馬太卻明確地說，施洗約翰的門徒來質問耶穌關於禁食的問題（太9:14）。
根據本註釋所採用暫定的編年表，約翰是公元29年春初被監禁的，可能在公元30年逾越節前不久被處決（見太4:12；可6:14-29；路3:19,20註釋）。約翰的門徒可能是在他去世前幾個月提出禁食問題的。
**你的門徒倒不禁食。**文士們就這樣顯然盼望使迅速增多的門徒團體與他們的夫子疏遠。
18.en:
**The disciples of John.** [The Question About Fasting, Mark 2:18–22=Matt. 9:14–17=Luke 5:33–39. Major comment: Mark. See Middle Galilean Ministry; on parables pp. 203–207.]
**Used to fast.** Probably better, “were fasting.” Doubtless John’s disciples shared at least to some extent in his abstemious way of life (see Matt. 3:4), as is evidenced here by their fasting. It seems clear that they were, indeed, fasting at the very time they brought their question to Jesus.
An ancient Jewish treatise on fasting from the 1st century .., Megillath Ta‘anith, mentions Jews who at that time regularly fasted on the second and fifth days of the week, that is, Monday and Thursday (see Luke 18:12). Although Jewish tradition attributes this custom to the story that Moses began his 40-day fast on Mt. Sinai (see Ex. 34:28) on a Thursday and terminated it on a Monday, it seems probable that the observance of these two days as fasts actually arose from the desire to keep them as far as possible from the Sabbath, and at the same time not to have them too close together. See Strack and Billerbeck, Kommentar zum Neuen Testament, vol. 2, pp. 241-243.
Strack and Billerbeck, leading authorities on ancient Judaism, indicate that the exact motives behind these biweekly fasts are not entirely clear, but it seems probable that they arose through a desire on the part of particularly earnest people to seek to atone for the worldliness of the nation, which they felt was fast bringing on its destruction. In general among the ancient Jews fasting was undertaken by individuals in order to make good a misdeed or to ensure the favorable answer to a prayer or fulfillment of a wish. Indeed, many seem to have fasted because they believed such an act earned special merit for them before God.
These uses of fasting rested, of course, upon a misconception of the character of God and of the nature of righteousness. Too often fasting degenerated into a means of righteousness by works through which men hoped to appease an austere God and earn His favor, regardless of the state of their hearts. Centuries before the time of Jesus the prophets had denounced such ideas, declaring that God had come to abhor Israel’s fasts and other religious observances (Isa. 58:3–5; Zech. 7:5, 6).
There are times when the Christian needs keenness of thought and discriminating judgment; he may have important decisions to make, or may need to discern more clearly the will of God. Under such circumstances fasting can prove a great blessing. Such fasting may not necessarily mean complete abstinence from food, but a diet limited to the simple essentials for maintaining health and vigor. The Christian may, like Daniel, refrain from the use of “pleasant bread” (Dan 10:3). God is not honored and one’s Christian experience is not promoted by any practice that weakens the body or impairs the health. See Matt. 6:16.
**They come and say.** Those here designated are not clearly identified, nor is the Gospel of Luke clearer in this respect (see Luke 5:33). However, Matthew states definitely that it was the disciples of John the Baptist who plied Jesus with the query in regard to fasting (Matt. 9:14).
According to the tentative chronology adopted in this commentary, John had been imprisoned in the early spring of this year, .. 29, and probably was executed shortly before the Passover of .. 30 (see on Matt. 4:12; Mark 6:14–29; Luke 3:19, 20). His disciples raised their question on fasting probably not more than a few months before he died.
**Thy disciples fast not.** Thus the scribes apparently hoped to alienate the rapidly growing body of disciples from their Master.

19.zh:
耶穌對他們說：新郎和陪伴之人同在的時候，陪伴之人豈能禁食呢？新郎還同在，他們不能禁食。

**陪伴之人。**指婚宴的賓客。耶穌這裡所用的比喻源於《舊約》的預言；其中把耶和華與祂子民的關係描述為新郎與新娘的關係（賽62:5；參何1:2）。約翰也曾用這個比喻說明他與彌賽亞的關係（約3:25-30）。在這之前約一年左右，猶太領袖們曾設法在約翰和耶穌之間挑起紛爭。所以耶穌在施洗約翰的門徒面前使用這個簡要的比喻似乎是很有意義的。
耶穌絲毫沒有偏離祂親自藉著摩西吩咐以色列人的宗教要求。祂和法利賽人爭論的焦點是古人的遺傳，就是“難擔的重擔”（太23:4）。這些傳統的要求被抬到尊貴和重要的地位，有時甚至與摩西律法的真正精神想牴觸（太15:3-6；參《歷代願望》395頁）。文士和法利賽人努力強加於百姓的宗教形式，就這樣使他們的敬拜上帝成了“枉然”和無意義（可7:7）。見太23:2,3註釋。
耶穌如今在三個簡單的比喻中所闡明的，是祂的教訓與文士們教訓的不相容性。約翰的門徒雖然可能接受基督為彌賽亞（見約1:35-37），但至少仍堅持文士和法利賽人所推行的某些儀文（可2:18）。在婚宴賓客，就是“陪伴之人”的比喻中，基督為自己的門徒所受到不遵守遺傳的指控作了辯護。祂暗示儀文的慣例應服從更重要的事。然後耶穌用新酒（22節）和新布（21節）的例子，進一步說明了所涉及的基本原則──新舊教訓之間是不可調和的。祂在這裡解釋了為什麼他認為遵守拉比的儀文沒有任何價值。這三個比喻綜合起來，是要告訴施洗約翰的門徒們：如果他們真相信他們老師的教導，他們也會接受耶穌的教導。
**他們不能禁食。**如果婚宴賓客悲哀憂鬱，不肯吃宴席的話，就會被視為對新郎和新娘的侮辱。
19.en:
**Children of the bridechamber.** A contemporary Jewish idiom for wedding guests. The comparison Jesus used here has its roots in OT prophecy, where Jehovah’s relation to His people is depicted as that of the bridegroom to the bride (Isa. 62:5; cf. Hosea 1:2). John had already used the same figure to explain His relationship to the Messiah (ch. 3:25–30), upon the former occasion when the Jewish leaders had sought to drive a wedge of rivalry between John and Jesus, probably a year or so prior to this occasion. It seems significant, therefore, that Jesus used this brief figure in the presence of the disciples of John the Baptist.
In no particular did Jesus deviate from the religious requirements He Himself had enjoined on Israel through Moses. Contention between Himself and the Pharisees centered in the traditions of the elders, the “heavy burdens” that were “grievous to be borne” (Matt. 23:4). These traditional requirements had been elevated to a position of such honor and importance that at times they were allowed even to counteract the true spirit of the law of Moses (ch. 15:3–6; cf. DA 395). Thus the form of religion that the scribes and Pharisees sought to impose upon the people rendered their worship of God “vain” and meaningless (Mark 7:7). See on Matt. 23:2, 3.
What Jesus now set forth, in three brief figures, was the incompatibility of His teachings with those of the scribes. John’s disciples, although presumably accepting Christ as the Messiah (see John 1:35–37), nevertheless adhered at least to some of the ritual regulations imposed by the scribes and Pharisees (Mark 2:18). In the parable of the wedding guests, “the children of the bridechamber,” Christ defended His own disciples against the charge that they did not conform likewise to tradition. He implied that ritual practices were to be subordinated to concerns of higher importance. Then by the examples of the new wine (v. 22) and the new cloth (v. 21), Jesus developed still further the fundamental principle involved—the irreconcilable difference between the new teachings and the old. Here He explained why He considered rabbinical ritual observances as of no value. Taken together, these three parables were designed to make clear to the disciples of John the Baptist that if they truly believed the teachings of their master, they would accept His also.
**They cannot fast.** It would be considered an insult to the bride and groom should the wedding guests be mournful and gloomy and refuse to partake of the wedding feast.

20.zh:
但日子將到，新郎要離開他們，那日他們就要禁食。

**日子將到。**基督在這裡第一次公開暗示，祂最終會被帶離祂的門徒，就像新郎從婚宴上被帶走一樣。一年多前，祂曾私下告訴尼哥底母，祂要被“舉起來”（約3:14）。
**離開。**apairō，“提起”，“帶走”。在這裡該詞可能暗示被迫和痛苦的分離，比如耶穌的慘死。
祂在十字架上被“帶走”離開他們，並在復活後回到他們身邊。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第277頁。
20.en:
**The days will come.** Here for the first time Christ publicly implied that eventually He would be taken from His disciples, like a bridegroom forcibly taken from the wedding festivities. More than a year before this He had told Nicodemus in private that He would be “lifted up” (John 3:14).
**Taken away.** Gr. apairō, “to lift off,” “to carry away.” In the present context the word may imply forced and painful separation, as was true in the violent death of Jesus.
He was “taken away” from them at the cross, and restored to them after the resurrection.

21.zh:
沒有人把新布縫在舊衣服上，恐怕所補上的新布帶壞了舊衣服，破的就更大了。

**沒有人……縫。**見路5:36註釋。在這個比喻中，基督指出用祂教訓的“新布”去補猶太教的“舊衣服”是愚蠢的。
**新。**agnaphos，“未經梳理的”，所以是“新的”，這裡的意思是“未漂白的”或“未縮水的”。
**布。**或“補丁”。耶穌的教導決不是一塊要補在破舊的猶太教制度上的補丁。
**舊衣服。**這裡把猶太教比作一件舊衣服，已經無用，需要丟棄了。大多數遵守猶太教的人已經喪失了這個宗教起初的精神，而代之以一套形式的制度。基督設法用這個比喻向施洗約翰的門徒說明：把天國的好消息與猶太傳統的舊習慣交織在一起是徒勞的。
**破的就更大了。**就是補上補丁後衣服更糟糕了。改善這件舊衣服的初衷反而使它的缺陷更加明顯。
21.en:
**No man also seweth.** See on Luke 5:36. In this extended metaphor, or brief parable, Christ points out the folly of attempting to patch the old mantle of Judaism with the new fabric of His teachings.
**Piece.** Rather, “a patch.” Jesus’ teachings were not simply a patch to be applied to the worn-out Jewish religious system.
**New.** Gr. agnaphos, “uncarded,” hence, “new,” here meaning “unbleached,” or “unshrunk.”
**An old garment.** Here Judaism is compared to a worn-out cloak, one that has become useless and is on the point of being discarded. The original spirit of the Jewish religion had long since been lost by the majority of those who adhered to it, and in its place there had grown up a system of forms. By the use of this figure Christ endeavored to make clear to the disciples of John the Baptist the futility of trying to interweave the good news of the kingdom of heaven with the worn-out observances of Jewish tradition.
**Made worse.** That is, when the garment first becomes wet after the application of the patch. What is intended to improve the old mantle only serves to make its defects more evident.

23.zh:
耶穌當安息日從麥地經過。他門徒行路的時候，掐了麥穗。

這件事可能發生在公元29年春末的一個安息日，因為它與那段時期的事件記在一起。
**當安息日。**由於法利賽人在這裡對所走的路程沒有什麼異議，所以似乎最多走了一安息日的路程，即約有2裡（見本卷註釋第50頁）。
**從麥地經過。**或“在麥地旁邊”。門徒無疑沒有在麥子中間走，將麥子踩在腳下，而是沿著穿過麥地的一條小路行走。
**麥。**這裡要麼是小麥，要麼是大麥。路加（見路6:1）補充說門徒用手搓大麥或小麥，去掉麥殼。
23.en:
**It came to pass.** [Plucking Grain on the Sabbath, Mark 2:23–28=Matt. 12:1–8=Luke 6:1–5. Major comment: Mark. See Early Galilean Ministry.] This incident probably took place on a Sabbath day in the late spring of .. 29, since it is grouped with events of that period of time.
**Through the corn fields.** Or, “beside the fields of grain.” Undoubtedly the disciples were not walking through the grain, treading it down, but along a path that went through the fields.
**On the sabbath.** Inasmuch as the Pharisees here made no objection to the distance covered, it would seem that it was not more than a Sabbath day’s journey, that is, about 2/3 mi. (see p. 50).
**Of corn.** Literally, “of grain”; in this instance almost certainly either wheat or barley. Luke (see ch. 6:1) adds that the disciples began rubbing the barley or wheat in their hands to remove the hulls.

24.zh:
法利賽人對耶穌說：看哪，他們在安息日為什麼做不可做的事呢？

**法利賽人說。**這是從基督在加利利公開傳道以來，聖經第四次記錄祂遭遇文士和法利賽人（見6,16,18節；見路6:6註釋）。
**不可作的事。**只要不在安息日，門徒的這種行為在一週的任何一天無疑都不會遭到質疑，因為《舊約》的律法特別規定飢餓的人在過路時可以吃田裡的果子或穀物（見申23:24,25註釋）。
基督認可祂門徒這裡的做法，和祂自己在安息日的醫病之舉，常常被現代作家所誤解，作為祂自己不遵守關於安息日的舊約律法和規定，也不教導祂門徒遵守的證據。有人還主張基督對這些問題採取的立場應該被解釋為祂拒絕遵守第四條誡命。而事實上耶穌自己是堅持摩西的律法和十誡各方面要求，並教導祂門徒遵守的。祂多次確認道德律法的永恆約束力（見太5:17,18；約15:10等），並承認摩西的儀文律法適用當時的猶太人（見太23:3註釋）。當然，耶穌就是一個猶太人。
但是基督在地上的整個傳道過程中都與猶太領袖的人為律法和傳統產生衝突（見可7:2,3,8註釋）。基督同時代的許多人顯然把遵守這些要求看得比遵守摩西律法和十誡更加重要，基督對此採取不妥協的立場（見可2:19註釋）。這些要求，哪怕是最粗略的觀察，都會發現有許多顯然是荒謬的。然而法利賽人卻嚴厲地教導說：只有嚴格遵守這一切規條，才能得救。一個虔誠的猶太人努力在生活中不斷避免儀文上的不潔，而他所作的努力完全徒勞，因為人在不經意間就會違背這些儀文潔淨規條中的細節。這種靠行為稱義的制度與因信稱義是針鋒相對的。
《密西拿》列出了39種主要的在安息日禁止做的事（Shabbath 7. 2，《塔木德》松奇諾版，第348,349頁）。其中前11種是生產或製作糧食的步驟：播種，耕作，收割，捆紮，打穀，揚場，挑選（把不適合作食物的與適合作食物的分出來），碾磨，過篩，揉捏和烘烤。接下來是12種製作衣服的的相似步驟，從剪羊毛到縫紉衣服。再後的7個步驟，涉及食用鹿肉或用鹿皮作皮革等事項。其餘的項目涉及寫作、建築、點火，熄火、把物品從一處運到另一處。
這些一般性的規定得到進一步詳細的解釋。除了這些主要的規定之外，有關遵守安息日還有數不清的其它規定。最為人所知的就是所謂的“安息日路程”了，距離為2,000肘──2裡左右（見本卷註釋第50頁）。在安息日照牆上的鏡子也算違犯安息日（Shabbath149a, 《塔木德》松奇諾版第759頁），甚至連點亮一支蠟燭也算違犯安息日。但是同樣的規則卻允許在安息日將雞蛋賣給外邦人，並且允許僱外邦人來點蠟燭或點火。吐痰在地上被算為違法的，唯恐一葉小草得到澆灌。在安息日不可帶手帕，除非將它的一頭縫在衣服上，從技術上講，就不再是一塊手帕而是衣服的一部分了。關於一個人在安息日可以走的路程，類似的規定也可以避開它的限制，就是在沿途每隔一定的距離就儲藏一部分食物。從技術上講，儲藏食物的地方就算是主人的另一個“家了。從每一個這樣儲藏食物的地方都可以再走一個安息日的路程，到另一個類似的貯藏點。這只是基督時代虔誠的猶太人身上“難擔的重擔”（太23:4）的幾個例子。
法利賽人通過這種“蠓蟲就濾出來，駱駝倒吞下去”的做法，不斷地用人為律法的字句破壞上帝律法的精義。安息日起初原是給人機會通過學習創造主所造之物來認識祂，並反映祂的慈愛和良善，結果反倒使人想起法利賽人和文士自私專斷的品格。他們將上帝描畫為一個暴君，從而大大誤表了祂的品格。
大自然彰顯上帝的智慧、能力和慈愛。安息日起初的設立就是要使人注意這一切，免得人類專注於自己的活動而忘記了那創造他並不斷地為他的幸福和安寧運用神能的主。一旦明白了安息日的宗旨，現代一些基督徒在決定安息日做什麼合適、什麼不合適的問題時就容易解決了。凡使我們更接近上帝，幫助我們更好的明白祂對於我們的旨意和對待我們的方法，並使我們更有效地在我們的生活中及促進他人快樂與福利中與祂合作的事，都是真正遵守安息日（見賽58:13；可2:27,28註釋）。
24.en:
**Pharisees said.** This is Christ’s fourth recorded encounter with the scribes and Pharisees since the opening of His Galilean ministry (see vs. 6, 16, 18; see on Luke 6:6).
**Not lawful.** Upon any other day of the week than the Sabbath the action of the disciples would undoubtedly have passed unchallenged, for OT law specifically provided that a hungry person could eat of the fruit or grain of a field as he passed (see on Deut. 23:24, 25).
Christ’s approval of what His disciples did here, and His own acts of healing upon the Sabbath day, are often misunderstood by modern writers as proof that He neither observed personally nor taught His disciples to observe the OT laws and regulations in regard to Sabbath observance. Some also assert that the stand Christ took with regard to these matters is to be interpreted as a rejection by Him of the fourth commandment. The facts are that Jesus personally adhered to the requirements of the law of Moses and the Decalogue in every respect and taught His followers to do the same. He repeatedly affirmed the eternally binding nature of the moral law (see on Matt. 5:17, 18; John 15:10; etc.), and recognized also the validity of the ritual law of Moses as applicable to Jews at that time (see on Matt. 23:3). Jesus, of course, was a Jew.
But throughout His ministry on earth Christ was in conflict with the Jewish leaders over the validity of man-made laws and traditions (see on Mark 7:2, 3, 8). Toward these requirements, which apparently many of His contemporaries had come to regard as even more essential to piety than the laws of Moses and the Decalogue, Christ took a position of uncompromising opposition (see on ch. 2:19). The most cursory examination of many of these requirements makes their absurdity evident, yet the Pharisees sternly taught that salvation was to be obtained through the rigorous observance of all these rules. A pious Jew’s life tended to become one endless and vain effort to avoid ceremonial uncleanness, incurred when the least detail of these purely human requirements might have been disobeyed inadvertently. This system of righteousness by works was in mortal conflict with righteousness by faith.
The Mishnah lists 39 primary, or major, types of labor prohibited on the Sabbath day (Shabbath 7. 2, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, pp. 348, 349). The first 11 of these were steps leading to the production and preparation of bread: sowing, plowing, reaping, binding sheaves, threshing, winnowing, selecting (sorting what was unfit for food from what was fit), grinding, sifting, kneading, and baking. The next 12 apply to similar steps in the preparation of clothing, from the shearing of sheep to the actual sewing of garments. These are followed by 7 steps in preparing the carcass of a deer for use as food or for leather. The remaining items listed have to do with writing, building, the kindling and extinguishing of fires, and the transportation of articles from one place to another.
These general regulations were further explained in minute detail. In addition to these major regulations there were countless other provisions concerning the observance of the Sabbath. Most commonly known, perhaps, is the so-called “sabbath day’s journey” of 2,000 cu.— somewhat less than 2/3 mi. (see on p. 50). It was also counted as Sabbathbreaking to look in a mirror fixed to the wall (Shabbath 149a, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 759), or even to light a candle. Yet the same regulations permitted an egg laid on the Sabbath to be sold to a Gentile, and a Gentile to be hired to light a candle or a fire. It was counted unlawful to expectorate upon the ground, lest thereby a blade of grass be irrigated. It was not permissible to carry a handkerchief on the Sabbath, unless one end of it be sewed to one’s garment—in which case it was no longer technically a handkerchief but part of the garment. Similarly the regulation concerning the distance one might walk on the Sabbath day could be circumvented by hiding portions of food at appropriate intervals along the way one expected to take. Technically, then, the place where one’s food reposed could be considered as another “home” of the owner. From each such cache of food it was then possible to take another Sabbath day’s journey, on to the next similar cache. Such were but a few of the “heavy burdens and grievous to be borne” (Matt. 23:4) that had been placed upon the pious Jews of Christ’s day.
By thus straining at a gnat and swallowing a camel the Pharisees were continually employing the letter of man-made laws to destroy the spirit of the law of God. The Sabbath, designed originally to afford man an opportunity to know his Maker through a study of the things He had made, and to reflect upon His love and goodness, became, instead, a reminder of the selfish and arbitrary character of Pharisee and scribe. It effectively misrepresented the character of God, by picturing Him as a tyrant.
Nature declares the wisdom, power, and love of God, and it was to these things that the Sabbath was designed in the beginning to direct man’s attention, lest man become so absorbed in his own activities that he forget the One who gave him his being and who constantly exerted divine power for his happiness and welfare. The problem some modern Christians find in determining what may or may not be appropriate as a Sabbath activity is readily solved once the purpose of the Sabbath is clearly in mind. Whatever draws us closer to God, helps us to understand better His will for us and His ways of dealing with us, and leads us to cooperate more effectively with Him in our own lives and in contributing to the happiness and well-being of others—this is true Sabbath observance (see on Isa. 58:13; Mark 2:27, 28).

25.zh:
耶穌對他們說：經上記著大衛和跟從他的人缺乏飢餓之時所做的事，你們沒有念過嗎？

**缺乏飢餓時。**與聖所有關的律法和物品，原是為人的益處規定的。何時這些規定與人的最高利益，最大需要產生衝突，就必須置於從屬地位。
你們沒有讀過嗎？耶穌暗示他們在研究聖經時，沒有得到祂即將敘述的事中所含的教訓。
25.en:
**Have ye never read?** Jesus implies that in their study of the Scriptures they missed the lesson implicit in the incident He is about to relate.
**When he had need.** The sacred laws and things pertaining to the sanctuary had been ordained for the good of man, and if ever these should conflict with his best interests, with that which was most needful for him, they must be subordinated.

26.zh:
他當亞比亞他作大祭司的時候，怎麼進了神的殿，吃了陳設餅，又給跟從他的人吃。這餅除了祭司以外，人都不可吃。

**亞比亞他。**亞比亞他是亞希米勒的兒子。在這件事發生時，亞希米勒是掛名的大祭司（見撒上21:1,6）。耶穌的話似乎暗示亞比亞他代他年邁的父親的履行職責，所以實際上至少在他父親活著時，在父親的監管下，他履行大祭司的某些職能。亞希米勒被殺時，亞比亞他逃到了大衛那裡，隨身攜帶神聖的以弗得──大祭司職責的象徵（見撒上22:20）。在基督的時代也有類似的情況。當時該亞法擔任大祭司，但是亞拿則被大家公認為榮譽大祭司（見徒4:6；見路3:2註釋）。
**上帝的殿。**在這件事發生時，本節所提到的殿還沒有建造。“上帝的殿”只是帳幕，當時在挪伯。
**陳設餅。**見出25:30註釋。按製作和使用“陳設餅”的詳細規定，陳設餅分別為聖了。從聖所陳設餅的桌子上取下來的舊陳設餅，要由祭司在聖所範圍內吃掉（見利24:5-8註釋）。
**人都不可吃。**只有祭司可以吃這聖餅（見利24:9）。
26.en:
**House of God.** At the time of the incident here referred to the Temple had not yet been built. The “house of God” still consisted only of the tabernacle, at that time at Nob.
**Abiathar.** Abiathar was the son of Ahimelech, who was titular high priest at the time this incident occurred (see 1 Sam. 21:1, 6). The words of Jesus seem to suggest that Abiathar was deputy to his aging father and so actually performing at least some of the functions of the high priestly office even during the latter’s lifetime, and under his supervision. When Ahimelech was slain Abiathar fled to David, carrying with him the sacred ephod, symbol of the high priestly office (see 1 Sam. 22:20). An analogous situation prevailed in Christ’s day, when Caiaphas was high priest, but Annas was recognized by all as being a kind of high priest emeritus (see Acts 4:6; see on Luke 3:2).
**Shewbread.** See on Ex. 25:30. Elaborate rules for the preparation and use of the “bread of the Presence” set it apart as holy. The old bread, removed from the table of shewbread in the holy place, was to be eaten by the priests within the sacred precincts of the sanctuary (see on Lev. 24:5–8).
**Not lawful to eat.** None but the priests might eat the consecrated bread (see Lev. 24:9).

15.en:
**A large upper room.** Gr. anagaion, literally, any room above ground level, hence, a room in the upper part of the house. Compare the Gr. huperōon, which strictly means “upper room” (Acts 1:13; etc.). For a suggested identification of this room see on Matt. 26:18.
**Furnished.** Literally “spread.” Here, the reference is probably to the arrangement of the couches or cushions in the room (see on ch. 2:15).
**Prepared.** In anticipation, presumably, of the Passover.
15.zh:
他必指給你們擺設整齊的一間大樓，你們就在那裡為我們預備。

**一間大樓。**anagaion，直譯是在地面以上的任何房間，所以是房屋上層的房間。參希臘詞huperōon，它是嚴格意義上的“樓房”（徒1:13等）。關於這個房間的確認，見太26:18註釋。
**擺設整齊。**直譯是“擺開”。這裡大概指房間裡睡椅或臥榻的佈置（見可2:15註釋）。
**預備。**大概是預期逾越節的來到。

26.en: **Sung an hymn.** [Retirement to Gethsemane, Mark 14:26=Matt. 26:30=Luke 22:39. Major comment: Matthew.]
26.zh:
他們唱了詩，就出來，往橄欖山去。

[耶穌對彼得和其他十個門徒的警告：可14:27-31=太26:31-35=路22:31-38。註釋主要在《馬太福音》]。

17.en: **In the evening.** [The Celebration of the Passover, Mark 14:17, 18=Matt. 26:20=Luke 22:14–16. Major comment: Luke.] That is, the evening of “the first day of unleavened bread” (v. 12). For a discussion of the chronology of the Last Supper see Additional Notes on Matt. 26, Note 2.
17.zh:
到了晚上，耶穌和十二個門徒都來了。

**晚上。**就是“除酵節的前一天”的晚上（12節）。關於最後晚餐的時間順序，見《馬太福音》26章補充註釋二。
[ 揭露出賣主的人:可14:18b-21=太26:21-25=路22:21-23=約13:21-30。註釋主要在《馬太福音》和《約翰福音》] 。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–25節）**。《歷代願望》第652-661頁。

61.en: **The Blessed.** A designation for the Deity, to avoid use of the sacred name Jehovah, or Yahweh (see Vol. I, pp. 171, 172).
61.zh:
耶穌卻不言語，一句也不回答。大祭司又問他說：你是那當稱頌者的兒子基督不是？

**當稱頌者的。**指上帝，避免提耶和華或Yahweh（亞衛）的聖名（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷一第171,172頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（61–62節）**。見太26：63，64；路22：70懷愛倫註釋。

32.zh:
他們來到一個地方，名叫客西馬尼。耶穌對門徒說：你們坐在這裡，等我禱告。

**懷愛倫註釋（32–50節）**。《歷代願望》第685-697頁。

14.en:
**Goodman.** Gr. despotēs (see on Luke 2:29).
**Guestchamber.** Gr. kataluma, a word used in the papyri to describe any lodging place (see on Luke 2:7).
14.zh:
他進哪家去，你們就對那家的主人說：夫子說：客房在哪裡？我與門徒好在那裡吃逾越節的筵席。

**主人。**despotēs（見路2:29註釋）。
**客房。**kataluma，該詞在紙莎草文獻中表示任何可以寄宿的地方（見路2:7註釋）。

40.en: **Neither wist they.** A detail noted only by Mark. For similar situation, in which the disciples were speechless, see ch. 9:6.
40.zh:
又來見他們睡著了，因為他們的眼睛甚是睏倦；他們也不知道怎麼回答。

**他們也不知道。**只有馬可提到這個細節。關於門徒不說話的類似情形，見可9:6。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第690頁；見太26：43懷愛倫註釋。

11.en:
**They were glad.** Possibly the offer made by Judas came just at the time when they were ready to give up of immediately putting into effect their plans (see on Matt. 26:15).
**Conveniently.** See on Matt. 26:5; cf. Mark 14:2.
11.zh:
他們聽見就歡喜，又應許給他銀子；他就尋思如何得便把耶穌交給他們。

**他們就歡喜。**也許正當他們準備放棄立即實施自己的計劃時，猶大前來提出這個建議（見太26:15註釋）。
**得便。**見太26:5註釋；參可14:2。
[ 預備逾越節：可14:12-16=太26:17-19=路22:7-13。註釋主要在《馬太福音》] 。

41.en: **It is enough.** In the papyri the Greek word thus translated appears on receipts indicating payment in full (see on Matt. 6:2). Perhaps Jesus here means that the disciples had slept long enough. Or, He may have meant that the discussion of that particular matter was at an end.
41.zh:
第三次來，對他們說：現在你們仍然睡覺安歇吧（或作嗎？）！夠了，時候到了。看哪，人子被賣在罪人手裡了。

**夠了。**在紙莎草文獻中，“夠了”這個希臘詞出現在表示已完全支付的收據上（見太6:2註釋）。耶穌在這裡的意思可能是說門徒們已經睡得夠久了，也可能指對那個特殊問題的討論結束了。

53.en: **Led Jesus away.** [Night Trial Before the Sanhedrin, Mark 14:53–72=Matt. 26:57–75=Luke 22:54–65=John 18:25–27. Major comment: Matthew.]
53.zh:
他們把耶穌帶到大祭司那裡，又有眾祭司長和長老並文士都來和大祭司一同聚集。

**懷愛倫註釋（53–72節）**。《歷代願望》第698-715頁。

35.en: **The hour.** That is, the events of the hour.
35.zh:
他就稍往前走，俯伏在地，禱告說：倘若可行，便叫那時候過去。

**那時候。**指那時的事件。

27.en:
**Ye shall be offended.** [A Warning to Peter and the Ten, Mark 14:27–31=Matt. 26:31–35=Luke 22:31–38. Major comment: Matthew.]
**Because of me this night.** Textual evidence favors the omission (cf. p. 146) of these words here, but they are will attested in Matt. 26:31.
27.zh:
耶穌對他們說：你們都要跌倒了，因為經上記著說：我要擊打牧人，羊就分散了。

有文本在“你們都要跌倒”之前有“今晚為我的緣故”。太26:31證明有這句話。
**懷愛倫註釋（27–29節）**。《基督比喻實訓》第152頁；《歷代願望》第688頁。

18.en: **As they sat.** [The Betrayer Revealed, Mark 14:18b–21=Matt. 26:21–25=Luke 22:21–23=John 13:21–30. Major comment: Matthew and John.] Rather, “as they reclined” (see on ch. 2:15).
18.zh:
他們坐席正吃的時候，耶穌說：我實在告訴你們，你們中間有一個與我同吃的人要賣我了。

**他們坐席正吃的時候。**或“他們斜靠著的時候”（見可2:15註釋）。

14.22: **As they did eat.** [The Lord’s Supper, Mark 14:22–25=Matt. 26:26–29=Luke 22:17–20. Major comment: Matthew.]

54.en: **Fire.** Literally, “light.” It was the light of the fire doubtless that revealed Peter.
54.zh:
彼得遠遠的跟著耶穌，一直進入大祭司的院裡，和差役一同坐在火光裡烤火。

**火光。**無疑指照出彼得的火光。

14.12: **Killed the passover.** [Preparation for the Passover, Mark 14:12–16=Matt. 26:17–19=Luke 22:7–13. Major comment: Matthew.]

30.en:
**This day.** According to Jewish reckoning the sixth day of the week had already begun, at sunset, and the trial and crucifixion would take place before the following sunset.
**Twice.** Only Mark notes this detail.
30.zh:
耶穌對他說：我實在告訴你，就在今天夜裡，雞叫兩遍以先，你要三次不認我。

**今天。**依照猶太人的算法，這一週的第六日在日落時已經開始了，耶穌受審與被釘將發生在第二天日落之前。
**兩遍。**這個細節只有馬可提到。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第712頁。

13.en: **A man.** Apparently a servant, not the master of the house (see v. 14). It was unusual for man to carry water in a “pitcher” or earthenware jar; this was usually done by the womenfolk. Men generally transported water in warterskins.
13.zh:
耶穌就打發兩個門徒，對他們說：你們進城去，必有人拿著一瓶水迎面而來，你們就跟著他。

**有人。**顯然是僕人，而不是房子的主人（見14節）。男人用“瓶”或瓦罐盛水是不尋常的；通常這是女人乾的。男人一般用水袋運水。

1.zh:
過兩天是逾越節，又是除酵節，祭司長和文士想法子怎麼用詭計捉拿耶穌，殺他。

**懷愛倫註釋**。見太26：2懷愛倫註釋。
1.en: **After two days.** [The Betrayal Plot, Mark 14:1, 2, 10, 11=Matt. 26:1–5, 14–16=Luke 22:1–6=John 12:10, 11. Major comment: Matthew.]

2.zh:
只是說：當節的日子不可，恐怕百姓生亂。

[西門的筵席：可14:3-9=太26:6-13=路7:36-50=約12:1-9。註釋主要的《馬太福音》和《路加福音》] 。

3.zh:
耶穌在伯大尼長大痲瘋的西門家裡坐席的時候，有一個女人拿著一玉瓶至貴的真哪噠香膏來，打破玉瓶，把膏澆在耶穌的頭上。

**懷愛倫註釋（3–11節）**。《歷代願望》第557-568頁。
3.en: **Being in Bethany.** [Simon’s Feast, Mark 14:3–9=Matt. 26:6–13=Luke 7:36–50=John 12:1–9. Major comment: Matthew and Luke.]

6.zh:
耶穌說：由他吧！為什麼難為他呢？他在我身上做的是一件美事。

**懷愛倫註釋（6–8節）**。《歷代願望》第560頁。

7.zh:
因為常有窮人和你們同在，要向他們行善隨時都可以；只是你們不常有我。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》第161頁；《服務真詮》第201，205頁；《先知與君王》第652頁；《證言》卷四第552頁。

8.zh:
他所做的，是盡他所能的；他是為我安葬的事把香膏預先澆在我身上。

**盡她所能做的。**就是她充分利用了手頭所有的。這是上帝對每一個人的期待，不多也不少。
8.en: **Done what she could.** That is, she made the best use of what she had at hand. That is what God expects of everyone, no more and no less.

9.zh:
我實在告訴你們，普天之下，無論在什麼地方傳這福音，也要述說這女人所做的，以為記念。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷四第551頁。

10.zh:
十二門徒之中，有一個加略人猶大去見祭司長，要把耶穌交給他們。

**懷愛倫註釋（10–11節）**。見太26：14－16；路22：3－5懷愛倫註釋。

16.zh:
門徒出去，進了城，所遇見的正如耶穌所說的。他們就預備了逾越節的筵席。

[ 慶祝逾越節：可14:17,18a=太26:20=路22:14-16。註釋主要在《路加福音》] 。

21.zh:
人子必要去世，正如經上指著他所寫的；但賣人子的人有禍了！那人不生在世上倒好。

[ 主的晚餐：可14:22-25=太26:26-29=路22:17-20。註釋主要在《馬太福音》] 。

25.zh:
我實在告訴你們，我不再喝這葡萄汁，直到我在神的國裡喝新的那日子。

[ 前往客西馬尼園：可14:26=太26:30=路22:39。註釋主要在《馬太福音》] 。

29.zh:
彼得說：眾人雖然跌倒，我總不能。

**懷愛倫註釋（29–31節）**。《歷代願望》第673頁；見太26：31－35懷愛倫註釋。

31.zh:
彼得卻極力的說：我就是必須和你同死，也總不能不認你。眾門徒都是這樣說。

[ 客西馬尼園：可14:32-52=太26:36-56=路22:40-53=約18:1-12。註釋主要在《馬太福音》] 。

34.zh:
對他們說：我心裡甚是憂傷，幾乎要死；你們在這裡等候，警醒。

**懷愛倫註釋（34–38節）**。《證言》卷八第100頁。

36.zh:
他說：阿爸！父啊！在你凡事都能；求你將這杯撤去。然而，不要從我的意思，只要從你的意思。

**懷愛倫註釋**。見太26：42；路22：42；羅8：11懷愛倫註釋。

37.zh:
耶穌回來，見他們睡著了，就對彼得說：西門，你睡覺嗎？不能警醒片時嗎？

**懷愛倫註釋（37–38節）**。《歷代願望》第689頁。

38.zh:
總要警醒禱告，免得入了迷惑。你們心靈固然願意，肉體卻軟弱了。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第126頁；《早期著作》第167頁；《傳道良助》第163頁；《先祖與先知》第689頁；《論節制》第192頁；《證言》卷二第49，89，101，490頁；511頁；《證言》卷三第476頁；《證言》卷五第34，115，146頁；《證言》卷六第410頁。

50.zh:
門徒都離開他，逃走了。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第697頁。

51.zh:
有一個少年人，赤身披著一塊麻布，跟隨耶穌，眾人就捉拿他。

**有一個少年人。**這個表面上的區區小事似乎與那天晚上發生的大事沒有任何特別的關係，但靈感之筆將它包括在敘述之中必有一定的理由。有人認為本福音書的作者約翰·馬可（見徒12:12）在這裡暗中把自己與耶穌的被捕聯繫起來。這個“少年人”幾乎不可能是門徒中的一員，因為他們都已離開祂逃跑了（可14:50）。然而應該指出，關於這個少年人身份的任何說法雖然看上去可能合理，但都只是猜測。參約翰故意不提自己的名字（約21:20-24）。
**眾人。**有文本是“他們”。
51.en:
**A certain young man.** This apparently trivial incident does not appear to have any particular connection with the events of the night, yet Inspiration must have had some reason for including it in the narrative. It has been suggested that the author of the Gospel, John Mark (see Acts 12:12), here refers cryptically to his own connection with the arrest of Jesus. This “young man” can hardly have been one of the disciples, for they had all already forsaken Him and fled (Mark 14:50). It should be pointed out, however, that any suggestion regarding the identity of the young man is no more than a conjecture, reasonable though it may appear. Compare John’s studied failure to identify himself by name (John 21:20–24).
**The young men.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the simple reading “they.”
**52 Naked.** Perhaps completely so, or more likely, clad only in his undergarment, or tunic (see on Matt. 5:40; John 21:7).

52.zh:
他卻丟了麻布，赤身逃走了。

**赤身。**可能完全赤身，但更可能只穿著內衣或外套（見太5:40；約21:7註釋）。
[ 夜間在公會前受審：可14:53-72=太26:57-75=路22:54-65=約18:25-27。註釋主要在《馬太福音》] 。

56.zh:
因為有好些人作假見證告他，只是他們的見證各不相合。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》第71頁。

58.zh:
我們聽見他說：我要拆毀這人手所造的殿，三日內就另造一座不是人手所造的。

**懷愛倫註釋（58–60節）**。《歷代願望》第706頁。

63.zh:
大祭司就撕開衣服，說：我們何必再用見證人呢？

**懷愛倫註釋**。見太26：65懷愛倫註釋。

70.zh:
彼得又不承認。過了不多的時候，旁邊站著的人又對彼得說：你真是他們一黨的！因為你是加利利人。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第712頁。

72.zh:
立時雞叫了第二遍。彼得想起耶穌對他所說的話：雞叫兩遍以先，你要三次不認我。思想起來，就哭了。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第152頁。

2.en:
**Sabbath day.** As upon the previous visit (Luke 4:16).
**In the synagogue.** As upon the previous occasion (see on Luke 4:16). For a description of a Jewish synagogue and of the synagogue service see pp. 56, 57.
**Astonished.** Evidently it seemed incredible to the people of Nazareth that One who had lived among them could be the Son of God.
**This man.** Literally, “this [fellow],” an expression often denoting contempt.
**What wisdom is this?** See on Isa. 11:2, 3; 50:4. Neither the Jewish leaders nor the townspeople of Nazareth appear to have thought of denying the infinitely superior intelligence, understanding, and wisdom of Jesus. It was altogether too obvious; in fact, it was this that troubled them.
**Even such mighty works.** See p. 208. The people of Nazareth could not deny the great miracles Jesus wrought any more than they could deny His wisdom. Whether He taught or worked miracles, they were constrained to admit that “he hath done all things well” (ch. 7:37).
2.zh:
到了安息日，他在會堂裡教訓人。眾人聽見，就甚希奇，說：這人從哪裡有這些事呢？所賜給他的是什麼智慧？他手所做的是何等的異能呢？

**安息日。**與前一次訪問一樣（路4:16）。
**在會堂裡。**與上一次一樣（見路4:16註釋）。關於猶太會堂及其崇祀，見本卷註釋第56,57頁。
**甚希奇。**拿撒勒人顯然難以相信一個曾住在他們中間的人是上帝的兒子。
**這人。**一種輕蔑的稱呼。
這是什麼智慧？見賽11:2,3；50:4註釋。猶太領袖和拿撒勒居民似乎都有想要否認耶穌無限優越的知識，悟性和智慧。因為這太明顯了；實際上這正是令他們感到不安的原因。
**何等的異能。**見本卷註釋第208頁。拿撒勒人不能否認耶穌所行的偉大神蹟，也不能否認祂的智慧。無論是祂的教訓還是祂所行的神蹟，他們都不得不承認“祂所做的事都好”（可7:37）。

3.en:
**The carpenter.** Matthew reads, “the carpenter’s son” (ch. 13:55). Although in idiomatic Hebrew and Aramaic usage the expression “the carpenter’s son” may be no more than a circumlocution for “the carpenter,” there seems no reason to doubt that Joseph had been a carpenter by trade, and that prior to the time He took up His lifework, Jesus followed that trade (cf. DA 109). This, indeed, is one of the few NT side lights on Christ’s life between His childhood visit to the Temple and His baptism (see on Luke 2:51, 52).
**Son of Mary.** The fact that Jesus is here referred to as the “son of Mary” rather than as the “son of Joseph” strongly implies that Joseph was dead (cf. DA 109). Concerning Joseph as the “father” of Jesus see on Matt. 1:21; Luke 2:33.
**Brother of James.** As to Jesus’ brothers, see on Matt. 1:18, 25; 12:46. Many have confused this James with James the son of Alphaeus, usually because of the garbled records of the early Church Fathers, or their own conclusions based on Gal. 1:19 and 2:9. The only certain mention of this James after the conversion of Jesus’ brothers (see Acts 1:14; cf. John 7:5) is in Gal. 1:19, possibly also Jude 1. James “the Lord’s brother” should not be confused with James the son of Alphaeus (see on Mark 3:18).
**Juda.** Probably the writer of the epistle of Jude, for he is identified as the “brother” of James, the only individual in the NT named Jude (or Juda) of whom such an identification is certain (see Jude 1; see on Mark 3:18).
**His sisters.** The plural indicates at least two, and leaves open the possibility of more.
**Were offended.** Gr. skandalizō, literally, “were tripped up” (see on Matt. 5:29).
3.zh:
這不是那木匠嗎？不是馬利亞的兒子雅各、約西、猶大、西門的長兄嗎？他妹妹們不也是在我們這裡嗎？他們就厭棄他（厭棄他：原文是因他跌倒）。

**那木匠。**《馬太福音》為：“木匠的兒子”（太13:55）。雖然在希伯來文和亞蘭文習語中，“木匠的兒子”只是“木匠”的委婉說法，但似乎沒有理由懷疑約瑟曾從事木匠行業；耶穌在開始祂一生的工作之前，也從事木匠行業（參《歷代願望》109頁）。這確實是《新約》中關於從耶穌童年訪問聖殿到祂受洗這段時期裡，側面提到祂生活的少數經文之一（見路2:51,52註釋）。
**馬利亞的兒子。**這裡說耶穌是“馬利亞的兒子”而不是“約瑟的兒子”，有力地暗示約瑟已經去世（參《歷代願望》109頁）。關於約瑟為耶穌的“父親”，見太1:21；路2:33註釋。
**雅各、約西、猶大、西門的長兄。**關於耶穌的兄弟，見太1:18,25；12:46註釋。許多人曾把這個雅各和亞勒腓的兒子雅各混淆起來，大都是由於早期教父們斷章取義的記錄，或他們自己根據加1:19和2:9作出的推論。耶穌的弟兄們悔改以後（見徒1:14；參約7:5），唯一明確地提及這個雅各的經文是加1:19，可能還有猶1。不要把“主的兄弟”雅各與亞勒腓的兒子雅各混淆起來（見可3:18註釋）。
**猶大。**可能是《猶大書》的作者，因為他被確認為雅各的“兄弟”。在《新約》中，只有這個猶大有這種明確的身份界定（見猶1；見可3:18註釋）。
**他妹妹們。**複數形式表明至少有兩個，也可能更多。
**因祂跌倒。**skandalizō，直譯是“被絆倒”（見太5:29註釋）。

13.en: **Anointed with oil.** Olive oil was commonly employed as a medication in ancient Palestine (cf. Luke 10:34), and was used both internally and externally. The literal use of oil as a medication may have provided the basis for its symbolic use here and later on in the Christian church. Anointing with oil as an act of faith is mentioned only here and in James 5:14.
13.zh:
又趕出許多的鬼，用油抹了許多病人，治好他們。

**用油抹了。**在古代巴勒斯坦，橄欖油一般被用作藥物（參路10:34），既可內服也可外用。油的實際藥用可能為這裡和後來基督教會中的象徵性用法提供根據。抹油作為一種信心之舉只在本節和雅5:14中提到。
[ 施洗約翰的殉道：可6:14-29=太14:1,2,6-12=路9:7-9。註釋主要在《馬可福音》。見本卷註釋231頁圖表]。

4.en:
**A prophet.** See on Gen. 20:7; Deut. 18:15.
**Not without honour.** Christ’s statement seems to have been a commonly known proverb. If Jesus’ own brothers did not believe Him to be the Messiah (see John 7:5), how could His former neighbors be expected to believe?
**His own country.** The people of Nazareth knew Him well (see on Luke 2:52). All of His daily contacts with them testified to His perfection of character, and this they had resented because it placed them in an unfavorable light. In His exemplary character they had seen nothing that particularly appealed to them, nothing that they appreciated or considered of value to them in achieving the objectives for which they lived.
**His own kin.** Even a year later His brothers had not come to believe in Him (see on John 7:5), though they were converted after His death and resurrection (see on Acts 1:14).
4.zh:
耶穌對他們說：大凡先知，除了本地、親屬、本家之外，沒有不被人尊敬的。

**先知。**見創20:7；申18:15註釋。
**本地。**拿撒勒人很熟悉祂（見路2:52註釋）。祂與他們所有的日常接觸，都證明祂品格的完美，這是他們所討厭的，因為這使他們處在一種不愉快的亮光中。在祂模範的品格中，他們看不到有什麼特別吸引他們的地方。他們也不賞識或考慮這種品格在達到他們的生活目標方面對於他們的價值。
**親屬。**甚至一年以後，祂的兄弟們還沒有相信祂（見約7:5註釋），但在祂受死和復活以後，他們悔改了（見徒1:14註釋）。
**沒有不被人尊敬。**基督的話似乎是一個眾所周知的諺語。如果耶穌自己的兄弟們都不相信祂是彌賽亞（見約7:5），怎麼能指望祂從前的鄉鄰們相信祂呢？

1.zh:
耶穌離開那裡，來到自己的家鄉；門徒也跟從他。

**耶穌離開那裡。**根據馬太的記錄，耶穌第二次被拿撒勒人拒絕發生在海邊佈道之後，但沒有說多久以後（見太13:53,54；參《歷代願望》241頁）。馬太將耶穌在拿撒勒第二次遭到拒絕與施洗約翰的死緊密聯繫在一起（見太13:53至14:12）。馬可將第三次加利利旅行佈道與施洗約翰的死聯繫在一起（見可6:1-30；參《歷代願望》360頁）。施洗約翰的死一定發生在開始這次旅行佈道前後不久，因為正是十二使徒在加利利第三次旅行佈道的工作，使希律以為施洗約翰復活了（見14節註釋）。所以這最後一次訪問拿撒勒（見《歷代願望》241頁），可能發生在公元30-31年冬天。
**自己的家鄉。**關於耶穌在加利利傳道期間第一次訪問拿撒勒的大概時間，見《路加福音》第4章補充註釋。顯然只有確認兩次訪問，才能把福音書的記錄協調起來。關於這第二次訪問，馬太和馬可都沒有提拿撒勒的名字，但是這裡所說耶穌“自己的家鄉”無疑是指拿撒勒（見路4:16；參路2:51），因為耶穌是在拿撒勒長大的，祂曾住在那裡，開始祂畢生的工作（見可1:9）。那裡也是祂父母的家（見路2:1-5）。耶穌離開拿撒勒進行傳道以後，直到祂開始在加利利工作，才再次訪問拿撒勒。時間已經過去大約18個月（見路4:16註釋），大概從公元27年秋到公元29年春（見太4:12註釋）。在加利利的傳道大體上從公元29年春持續到公元30年春。所以這第二次也是最後一次訪問拿撒勒發生在這段時間的最後（參《歷代願望》241頁）。
1.en:
**He went out.** [Second Rejection at Nazareth, Mark 6:1–6=Matt. 13:54–58. Major comment: Mark. See Closing Galilean Ministry; a Synopsis of the Life of Christ.] According to Matthew’s account, the second rejection of Jesus by the people of Nazareth occurred after the Sermon by the Sea, though how long after is not stated (see Matt. 13:53, 54; cf. DA 241). Matthew closely links the second rejection at Nazareth with the death of John the Baptist (see chs. 13:53 to 14:12). Mark gives it in connection with events of the Third Galilean Tour and with the death of John the Baptist (see Mark 6:1–30; cf. DA 360). The Baptist’s death must have come either shortly before or after the beginning of the tour, for it was the work of the Twelve on the Third Galilean Tour that led Herod to think that John the Baptist had come to life (see on v. 14). Thus it is likely that this final visit to Nazareth (see DA 241) took place in the winter of .. 30–31.
**His own country.** For a discussion of the probable time of Jesus’ first visit to Nazareth during the period of His Galilean ministry see Additional Note on Luke 4. Apparently the only way the gospel record can be harmonized is on the basis of two visits. Neither Matthew nor Mark mentions Nazareth by name in connection with this, the second visit, but there can be no doubt that Nazareth is here appropriately referred to as Jesus’ “own country” by virtue of the fact that He had been brought up there (see Luke 4:16; cf. ch. 2:51), that He was living there at the time He had taken up His lifework (see Mark 1:9), and that it was His parents’ home (see Luke 2:1–5). After leaving Nazareth to take up His ministry Jesus did not revisit it until He began His Galilean ministry. The time elapsed was about 18 months (see on Luke 4:16), probably from the autumn of .. 27 to the spring of .. 29 (see on Matt. 4:12). The Galilean ministry as a whole continued from the spring of .. 29 to the spring of .. 30. Thus it was toward the close of this period that the second and final visit to Nazareth took place (cf. DA 241).

5.zh:
耶穌就在那裡不得行什麼異能，不過按手在幾個病人身上，治好他們。

**不得行什麼異能。**耶穌受到阻礙，不是因為祂缺乏能力，而是因為百姓缺乏信心（見太13:58）。
**幾個病人。**耶穌顯然只醫治一些較小的疾病，沒有施行祂在其他地方所行的顯著神蹟。
5.en:
**No mighty work.** Jesus was hindered, not by any lack of power on His part, but by the people’s lack of faith (see Matt. 13:58).
**A few sick folk.** Healed, apparently, of minor maladies. But there were no remarkable miracles such as Jesus had performed elsewhere.

6.zh:
他也詫異他們不信，就往周圍鄉村教訓人去了。

**祂也詫異。**幾個月以前，耶穌曾“詫異”那個百夫長的信心（見太8:10）。
**就往周圍鄉村教訓人去了。**也許是十二使徒在加利利各城市鄉村旅行傳道期間。馬可在提到十二使徒之前記錄了耶穌個人的傳道活動（見7節）。馬太則顛倒了這個順序（見太11:1）。
[ 第三次在加利利旅行傳道：可6:7-13=太9:36 to 11:1=路9:1-6。註釋主要的《馬太福音》]。
6.en:
**He marvelled.** A few months before this Jesus had “marvelled” at the faith of the centurion (see Matt. 8:10).
**He went.** Probably while the Twelve were making their circuit of the towns and villages of Galilee. Mark records Jesus’ personal evangelistic activities before mentioning those of the Twelve (see v. 7), whereas Matthew follows the reverse order (see Matt. 11:1).

7.zh:
耶穌叫了十二個門徒來，差遣他們兩個兩個的出去，也賜給他們權柄，制伏汙鬼；

**叫了十二個門徒來。**關於這十二個門徒最初的蒙召與任命，見可3:13-19註釋。
**兩個兩個地。**見可3:14註釋。
**權柄。**exousia，“權威”（見可2:10；路1:35註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第350頁；《佈道論》第72頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–11節）**。《歷代願望》第349-358頁。
7.en:
**Called unto him the twelve.** [Third Galilean Tour, Mark 6:7–13=Matt. 9:36 to 11:1=Luke 9:1–6. Major comment: Matthew.] For the original call and appointment of the Twelve see on ch. 3:13–19.
**By two and two.** See on ch. 3:14.
**Power.** Gr. exousia, “authority” (see on Mark 2:10; Luke 1:35).

8.zh:
並且囑咐他們：行路的時候不要帶食物和口袋，腰袋裡也不要帶錢，除了柺杖以外，什麼都不要帶；

錢包。直譯是“腰帶”（見太10:9註釋）。

9.zh:
只要穿鞋，也不要穿兩件掛子，

**褂子。**直譯是“外衣”或“襯衫”（見太10:10註釋）。

11.zh:
何處的人不接待你們，不聽你們，你們離開那裡的時候，就把腳上的塵土跺下去，對他們作見證。

有文本在本節最後還有“我實在告訴你們，當審判的日子，所多瑪和蛾摩拉所受的，比那城還容易受呢！”實在。見太5:18註釋。
11.en: **Verily.** See on Matt. 5:18. Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the omission of the remainder of v. 11.

12.zh:
門徒就出去傳道，叫人悔改，

**叫人悔改。**約翰（太3:2）和耶穌（見可1:15）都曾宣傳這個信息。十二個使徒既提供身體的醫治，也提供心靈的醫治。
12.en: **Men should repent.** The same message John (see Matt. 3:2) and Jesus (see Mark 1:15) had both preached. The Twelve were to offer healing for the soul as well as for the body.

14.zh:
耶穌的名聲傳揚出來。希律王聽見了，就說：施洗的約翰從死裡復活了，所以這些異能由他裡面發出來。

**希律王。**馬太提到大希律的兒子希律安提帕，是在羅馬權下加利利和比哩亞的統治者（見太2:22；路3:1）。馬太（太14:1）和路加都提到希律安提帕的稱號：“分封的王”（見路3:1註釋）。他只是羅馬所任命的“王”，而且“王”的稱呼只是出於一種禮儀。他在父親大希律死後，於公元前4年到公元39年統治他的領地。他的母親馬爾塔斯是撒瑪利亞人，也是亞基老的母親（見太2:22註釋）。他的官邸可能在提比哩亞，是他在加利利海西南海岸建造的一座城，以當時在位的凱撒提庇留的名字命名。見本卷註釋第64頁；40，234頁圖表。
**聽見了。**十二使徒在第三次加利利旅行傳道時所進行廣泛工作，顯然足以喚起人們對耶穌及其工作的普遍關注，並引起了希律的恐懼，以為耶穌是約翰從死裡復活了。前兩次佈道旅行都只是一組人在鄉村間活動，現在卻有七組了。顯然有報告從四面八方傳到了希律那裡，表明福音的迅速擴張。過去耶穌在當局看來只不過是一名孤獨的巡迴佈道者，由一夥成分複雜的門徒陪伴著，現在祂則顯示出遠為廣泛的活動範圍，希律不會再聽不到祂的消息了。
**施洗約翰復活了。**迷信加上問心有愧使希律得出了這個結論。
**異能。**見本卷註釋第208頁註釋。約翰沒有行過神蹟（約10:41）。
14.en:
**King Herod.** [Martyrdom of John the Baptist, Mark 6:14–29=Matt. 14:1, 2, 6–12=Luke 9:7–9. Major comment: Mark. See The Ministry of Our Lord ] Matthew mentions Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great and ruler of Galilee and Peraea by authority of Rome (see on Matt. 2:22; Luke 3:1). Both Matthew (ch. 14:1) and Luke refer to Herod Antipas by his official title, “tetrarch” (see on Luke 3:1). He was “king” only by Roman appointment, and the title “king” was permitted only as a courtesy. He ruled over his territory from the death of his father, Herod the Great, in 4 .., to .. 39. His mother was Malthace, a Samaritan, who was also the mother of Archelaus (see on Matt. 2:22). His official residence was probably at Tiberias, a city he built on the southwestern shore of the Lake of Galilee and named after the then-ruling Caesar, Tiberius. See p. 64; The Hasmonaeans and the Herods and Palestine Under the Herodians.
**Heard of him.** The extensive labors of the Twelve during the course of the Third Galilean Tour were evidently sufficient to call widespread attention to Jesus and His work, and to stir the fear of Herod that Jesus was John risen from the dead. Whereas on the two previous evangelistic expeditions there had been but one group going from village to village, now there were seven. Evidently the reports coming to Herod, from all quarters, revealed a rapid extension of the gospel. Whereas in the past Jesus may have appeared to the authorities to be no more than a solitary itinerant preacher accompanied by a motley group of followers, it was now evident that He represented a far larger movement. Herod could no longer help hearing of him.
**John the Baptist was risen.** It seems to have been superstition combined with a guilty conscience that led Herod to this conclusion.
**Mighty works.** See p. 208. John had performed no miracles (John 10:41).

15.zh:
但別人說：是以利亞。又有人說：是先知，正像先知中的一位。

**別人說。**見可8:27,28；路9:19。
**以利亞。**《舊約》關於以利亞回來的預言，見賽40:3-5；瑪3:1；4:5,6註釋。
**是先知，正像先知中的一位。**根據這些謠言，耶穌要麼是一位古代的先知復活了，要麼像他們中的一位。儘管約翰沒有行過神蹟（約10:41），連耶路撒冷的領袖們都接受他可能是一位先知的觀念（見約1:19-27註釋），更不要說一般的百姓了（見太14:5；21:26）。
15.en:
**Others said.** See Mark 8:27, 28; Luke 9:19.
**Elias.** That is, Elijah. Concerning the OT prophecies about the return of Elijah see on Isa. 40:3–5; Mal. 3:1; 4:5, 6.
**A prophet, or as one.** According to the rumors, Jesus was either one of the ancient prophets come to life or was like one of them. In spite of the fact that John performed no miracles (John 10:41), even the leaders in Jerusalem, to say nothing of people generally (see Matt. 14:5; 21:26), had entertained the idea that he might be a prophet (see on John 1:19–27).

16.zh:
希律聽見卻說：是我所斬的約翰，他復活了。

**約翰。**見14節註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第728頁。

17.zh:
先是希律為他兄弟腓力的妻子希羅底的緣故，差人去拿住約翰，鎖在監裡，因為希律已經娶了那婦人。

**他兄弟的妻子腓力。**不是腓力王（見路3:1,19註釋），而是大希律的另一個兒子，為馬利亞娜第二所生。希律安提帕是大希律的次子，由瑪爾塔斯所生，因此與這個腓力是同父異母的兄弟。希羅底是大希律的孫女，其父是大希律的另一個妻子馬利亞娜第一所生的兒子。希羅底原來嫁給她父親同父異母的兄弟腓力，後來又成了父親另一個同父異母的兄弟安提帕的妻子。見本卷註釋40頁圖表。
**希羅底。**見路3:19註釋。她原來嫁給腓力（見上文），後來因愛上希律安提帕，就與丈夫離婚了。希律則與阿拉比亞國王阿里塔斯的女兒離婚。所以希律和希羅底各有一個在世的配偶。由於希律與他的前妻離婚，他前妻的父親阿里塔斯就向希律發動了一次戰爭並擊敗了他。這次失敗被猶太人視為上帝對希律懲罰，因為他與希羅底的結合是不合理的（約瑟弗斯《猶太古代史》xviii. 5. 1,2）。
**鎖在監裡。**見路3:19,20註釋。約翰從公元29年逾越節之前（見《路加福音》第4章補充註釋）到接下來的冬天，可能關在瑪卡琉斯（Machaerus）的城堡裡（見路3:20註釋），不到一年時間。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–18節）**。《救贖的故事》第197頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–28節）**。《歷代願望》第214-225頁。
17.en:
**Bound him in prison.** See on Luke 3:19, 20. John had probably been in prison in the fortress of Machaerus (see on Luke 3:20) from before the Passover of .. 29 (see Additional Note on Luke 4) to the following winter, a little less than one year.
**Herodias’** See on Luke 3:19. Originally married to Philip (see below), she divorced him in preference for Herod Antipas. For his part, Herod had divorced the daughter of Aretas, king of Arabia. Thus Herod and Herodias each had a living spouse. As a result of Herod’s divorcing his former wife, her father, Aretas, made war on Herod and defeated him.
