**Very.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the reading “again.” This seems to imply that the feeding of the 5,000 is here referred to indirectly (see on Matt. 15:32).

10.zh:
隨即同門徒上船，來到大瑪努他境內。

[ 要求顯神蹟：可8:11-21=太16:1-12。註釋主要在《馬太福音》] 。

12.zh:
耶穌心裡深深的歎息，說：這世代為什麼求神蹟呢？我實在告訴你們，沒有神蹟給這世代看。

**深深地嘆息。**只有馬可提到這個細節。耶穌為他們感到失望，因為他們對屬靈真理的領悟非常遲鈍（見太16:9；可7:34註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第406，407頁。
12.en: **Sighed deeply.** A detail noted only by Mark. Jesus was disappointed at their slowness to perceive spiritual truth (see on Matt. 16:9; Mark 7:34).

14.zh:
門徒忘了帶餅；在船上除了一個餅，沒有別的食物。

**一個餅。**這個細節也只有馬可提到。
14.en: **One loaf.** Another detail noted only by Mark.

15.zh:
耶穌囑咐他們說：你們要謹慎，防備法利賽人的酵和希律的酵。

**希律的酵。**就是希律的邪惡影響，尤其是他的世故和優柔寡斷（見太13:33；16:6註釋）。在馬太的相應記錄中（太16:6），寫的是“撒都該人的酵”。由於撒都該人一貫謀求統治勢力的支持，迷戀世俗（見本卷註釋第52頁），他們的主要興趣與希律一樣，並向猶太民族解釋希律的政策。所以就一般意義和影響而言，馬太和馬可所使用的這兩個詞是可以互相替換的。
15.en: **Leaven of Herod.** That is, the evil influence of Herod, particularly his worldliness and vacillating character (see on Matt. 13:33; 16:6). In the parallel passage in Matthew (ch. 16:6) the Sadducees appear in the place of Herod. Inasmuch as the Sadducees consistently courted the favor of the ruling power and were themselves worldly-minded (see p. 52), their chief interests were closely identified with those of Herod, and they interpreted his policies to the Jewish nation. Thus, so far as general meaning and influence are concerned, the terms given in Matthew and Mark are interchangeable.

18.zh:
你們有眼睛，看不見嗎？有耳朵，聽不見嗎？也不記得嗎？

**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五第464頁。

21.zh:
耶穌說：你們還是不明白嗎？

[ 伯賽大附近的盲人：可8:22-26。見本卷註釋221頁地圖；231頁圖表；關於神蹟，見本卷註釋第208-213頁]。

22.zh:
他們來到伯賽大，有人帶一個瞎子來，求耶穌摸他。

**他們來到。**耶穌和門徒最近從抹大拉來到這裡（見太16:1,5註釋），這件事以後，繼續前往凱撒利亞腓立比（見可8:27；見太16:13註釋）。耶穌來到伯賽大（見太11:21註釋），再一次放棄了加利利，原因與祂幾周前退到腓尼基一樣（見太15:21；16:13註釋）。這次所行的神蹟在許多方面與不久前為那個聾啞患者所行的相似（見可7:31-37註釋）。
**有人帶來。**象低加波利的聾啞患者那樣（見可7:32註釋）。
22.en:
**He cometh.** [The Blind Man Near Bethsaida, Mark 8:22–26. See Retirement from Public Ministry; The Ministry of Our Lord; on miracles pp. 208–213.] Jesus and the disciples had recently arrived from Magdala (see on Matt. 16:1, 5), and after this incident, continued on their way to Caesarea Philippi (see Mark 8:27; see on Matt. 16:13). In coming to Bethsaida (see on Matt. 11:21), Jesus once more forsook Galilee, for the same reasons that had occasioned His withdrawal to Phoenicia a few weeks before this (see on Matt. 15:21; 16:13). The miracle performed upon this occasion resembles in many respects that performed for the deaf-mute in Decapolis not long previously (see on Mark 7:31–37).
**They bring.** As also in the case of the deaf-mute of Decapolis (see on ch. 7:32).

23.zh:
耶穌拉著瞎子的手，領他到村外，就吐唾沫在他眼睛上，按手在他身上，問他說：你看見什麼了？

**領他到村外。**這樣做可能至少有兩個原因：（1）避免公開（見26節註釋），（2）幫助這個盲人明白並專注於基督即將為他做的事情（參可5:37,40；7:33）。耶穌在公開傳道的這段時期，行神蹟似乎比較少，並且多半是在外邦人中行的。
**你看見什麼了。**這是記錄耶穌提這種問題的唯一事例，目的顯然是要加強這個人不完全的信心（見24節註釋）。
23.en:
**Led him out.** There were probably at least two reasons for this: (1) to avoid publicity (see on v. 26), and (2) in order to help the blind man understand and concentrate upon what Christ was about to do for him (cf. on chs. 5:37, 40; 7:33). Jesus seems to have performed comparatively few miracles during the period of His public ministry, and in most instances He was among a population that was largely heathen.
**If he saw ought.** This is the only recorded occasion on which Jesus asked such a question, and apparently it was done here with the objective of strengthening the man’s imperfect faith (see on v. 24).

24.zh:
他就抬頭一看，說：我看見人了；他們好像樹木，並且行走。

**他們好像樹木。**這是記錄耶穌分兩個階段治病的唯一事例。沒有明顯的原因解釋為何這次用這種方法。但值得注意的是，當這個人的恢復了部分視力的時候，他的信心就增長了，準備好相信耶穌能徹底治癒他（見23節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《佈道論》第594頁；《醫療佈道論》第98頁；《證言》卷一第462頁。
24.en: **Men as trees.** This is the only recorded instance in which Jesus performed a cure in two stages. There is no apparent reason for the use of this method in this case. However, it should be noted that, as partial vision was restored to the man, his faith increased and he was ready to believe that Jesus could cure him completely (see on v. 23).

25.zh:
隨後又按手在他眼睛上，他定睛一看，就復了原，樣樣都看得清楚了。

**按手。**見可7:33；8:23註釋。
**樣樣。**即“每一樣事物”。
**清楚了。**tēlaugōs，直譯是“遠處閃光的”，就是“在遠處而且清楚的”。有文本是dēlaugōs，意為“輝煌地”或“非常明亮地”。
25.en:
**Put his hands.** See on chs. 7:33; 8:23.
**Every man.** Better, “everything.”
**Clearly.** Gr. tēlaugōs, literally, “far shining,” that is “at a distance and clearly.” Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the reading dēlaugōs, “radiantly,” or “in full light.”

26.zh:
耶穌打發他回家，說：連這村子你也不要進去。

**這村子。**指伯賽大（見22節註釋）。這個人的家顯然不在耶穌叫他不要進去伯賽大。不讓他進去是避免這個神蹟的傳播，有利於耶穌的退隱（見22節註釋）。
[ 退到凱撒利亞腓立比：偉大的宣告：可8:27 至 9:1=太16:13-28=路9:18-27。註釋主要在《馬太福音》] 。
26.en: **The town.** That is, Bethsaida (see on v. 22). Apparently the man’s home was not in this city, which Jesus immediately told him not to enter. This restriction was evidently intended to prevent news of the miracle from spreading, and thus aid Jesus in His endeavor to secure retirement (see on v. 22).

27.zh:
耶穌和門徒出去，往該撒利亞腓立比的村莊去；在路上問門徒說：人說我是誰？

**懷愛倫註釋（27–38節）**。《歷代願望》410-418頁。
27.en: **Jesus went out.** [Withdrawal to Caesarea Philippi: The Great Confession, Mark 8:27 to 9:1=Matt. 16:13–28=Luke 9:18–27. Major comment: Matthew.]

31.zh:
從此，他教訓他們說：人子必須受許多的苦，被長老、祭司長，和文士棄絕，並且被殺，過三天復活。

**從此他教訓。**見太16:21註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《救贖的故事》第205頁。
31.en: **He began to teach.** For comment see on Matt. 16:21.

32.zh:
耶穌明明的說這話，彼得就拉著他，勸他。

**明明地。**就是“明確地”或“毫無保留地”。馬可不是說耶穌公開宣佈祂現在給門徒的教訓，而是說祂用清楚平實的語言跟他們討論這個教訓。
32.en: **Openly.** That is, “plainly,” or “without reserve.” Mark does not mean that Jesus made a public announcement of the lesson He now gave the disciples, but rather that He discussed it with them in plain, literal language.

34.zh:
於是叫眾人和門徒來，對他們說：若有人要跟從我，就當捨己，背起他的十字架來跟從我。

**眾人。**除了經常在耶穌身邊的門徒之外，顯然還有其他人，可能是聽說過祂的當地猶太居民（見太16:24註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第590頁；《佈道論》第90頁；《基督教育原理》第511頁；《證言》卷二第178頁；《證言》卷四第521，632頁；《證言》卷八第209頁；見太16：24；路9：23懷愛倫註釋。。
34.en: **People.** Literally, “crowd.” There were apparently others with Jesus besides His regular disciples, possibly Jewish residents of the region who had heard of Him (see on Matt. 16:24).

35.zh:
因為，凡要救自己生命（或作：靈魂；下同）的，必喪掉生命；凡為我和福音喪掉生命的，必救了生命。

**福音。**見可1:1註釋。這是馬可所記錄有關這件事的一個細節。耶穌在這裡把自己與自己的信息視為一體（見約6:51,63）。
35.en: **Gospel’s.** See on ch. 1:1. Only Mark has this detail of the story. Here Jesus identifies Himself with His message (see John 6:51, 63).

36.zh:
人就是賺得全世界，賠上自己的生命，有什麼益處呢？

**懷愛倫註釋（36–37節）**。《兒童教育指南》第329頁；《健康勉言》第593頁；《基督比喻實訓》第267頁；《給管家的勉言》第74，84頁；《教育論》第145頁；《佈道論》第559頁；《先知與君王》第274頁；《證言》卷一第706頁；《證言》卷二第59頁；《證言》卷三第250頁；《證言》卷六第78頁。

38.zh:
凡在這淫亂罪惡的世代，把我和我的道當作可恥的，人子在他父的榮耀裡，同聖天使降臨的時候，也要把那人當作可恥的。

**淫亂罪惡的世代。**見太11:16；12:39註釋。這是馬可所記錄有關這件事的又一個細節（見35節註釋）。
**可恥的。**見太10:32註釋；參羅1:16。
**榮耀。**顯然指基督復臨（見太25:31註釋）。接下來所記錄耶穌變像，乃是基督復臨的一個縮影（見太16:28註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第422頁；《證言》卷五第588頁。
38.en:
**Ashamed.** See on Matt. 10:32; cf. Rom. 1:16.
**Adulterous and sinful generation.** See on Matt. 11:16; 12:39. Another detail of this occasion recorded only by Mark (see on v. 35).
**The glory.** A clear reference to the second advent of Christ (see on Matt. 25:31), of which event the Transfiguration, which follows next in the record, was a miniature demonstration (see on Matt. 16:28).

8.11: **Pharisees came forth.** [The Demand for a Sign, Mark 8:11–21=Matt. 16:1–12. Major comment: Matthew.]

0.zh:
**一、卷名**
現有最早的文本僅註明為馬可所著。後來，當“福音”一詞用來表示基督生活和傳道的故事時，才把它加到該卷書的卷名中，成了《馬可福音》。英文欽定本中的卷名《聖馬可福音》只見於後來的文本中。
**二、作者**
基督教的傳統說法一致認為約翰馬可為《馬可福音》的作者。馬可是作者的姓（徒12:12,25），他名叫約翰（見徒13:5,13），他母親叫馬利亞（徒12:12）。他是巴拿巴的表弟（西4:10）。巴拿巴曾住在塞浦路斯（徒4:36）。馬可在耶路撒冷的居所似乎有樓層。耶穌復活和昇天以後，一些使徒至少有一段時間住在這裡（約20:19；徒1:13），早期教會的成員也在這裡聚會（徒12:12）。保羅和巴拿巴第一次外出傳道的頭一段路程中，約翰馬可曾陪伴他們（徒13:5,13）。後來，馬可陪巴拿巴去塞浦路斯（徒15:36-37）。再後，他似乎在彼得和保羅的指導下工作（彼前5:13；西4:10；提後4:11）。這卷福音書冠以象馬可這樣不很出名之人的名字，間接證明了其真實性，以及馬可的作者身份。這卷書如果是偽造的，就會冠以比較著名的、曾親身跟過耶穌之人的名字，如彼得。沒有充分的理由可以懷疑這卷書的真實性，以及馬可的作者身份。希拉波利的監督巴比亞斯（距小亞細亞的歌羅西和老底嘉有16公里）是已知第一位談到馬可為該書作者的作家。據尤西比烏斯所引，巴比亞斯在《註釋》一書中說：（《教會史》卷三 39.15）
“長老（最有可能是長老約翰）曾說過：‘馬可成為彼得的翻譯，把他所記憶的一切主的言行準確地寫下來，不過並沒有按照順序。因為他沒有聽過主講道，也沒有跟從過祂，而是以後如我所說的跟了彼得。彼得曾根據需要轉述主的言論，但沒有進行編排。所以，馬可把所記憶的各點記下來時並沒有差錯。他把注意力集中在一件事上，沒有遺漏他所聽見的話，也沒有記錯。’”
上面這段話同彼得稱馬可為“我的兒子”（彼前5:13）是吻合的。
一般認為，巴比亞斯的話暗示馬可擔任彼得的翻譯，因為彼得的母語是亞蘭語，而他顯然要前往不講亞蘭語的地區，向他不熟悉其方言的聽眾講道（見《使徒行述》40頁）。可以推定，馬可經常為彼得所傳福音翻譯，所以十分熟悉其中內容，從而為在聖靈感動下撰寫基督的生平作好了準備。大部分學者都認為馬可的記錄是四福音中最早的。
《馬可福音》究竟寫於彼得生前還是在死後，教父們意見不一（彼得殉道在公元64-66年左右）。里昂的伊裡奈烏斯（約公元185年）說《馬可福音》寫於彼得死後（《駁斥異端》卷三1.1）。亞歷山大的克萊門特則說寫於彼得生前（尤西比烏斯《教會史》卷六14.5-7）。後者的觀點似乎與現有的資料比較吻合。但不管怎樣，《馬可福音》的寫作年代無疑在公元55─70年之間。
馬可福音的許多用語證明它是為非猶太人寫的。象 Kentu--rion（百夫長，可15:39），spekoulator（護衛兵，可6:27）。這些拉丁詞暗示，雖然馬可是用文化語言希臘語寫的，其對象卻是羅馬人。馬可本來可以用普通希臘詞語而不用拉丁語來表示這些軍官的稱呼。可是他多次採用拉丁詞語的希臘譯文，可能是因為讀者比較熟悉的緣故。他解釋巴勒斯坦的硬幣，顯然是因為他的讀者不熟悉它（可12:42）。同樣，他解釋了猶太人的逾越節（可14:12）和法利賽人的習慣（可7:3,4），翻譯了若干亞蘭文的詞語（可5:41；可7:34；可15:34），這對於巴勒斯坦的讀者是不必要的。同時，作者又顯然是通曉亞蘭語和舊約聖經的猶太人。不過他所引用的《舊約》是七十士譯本。
**三、歷史背景**
見《馬太福音》註釋序言。
**四、主題**
《馬可福音》是四福音中最短的。可是在有些方面它又是寫得最生動最有力的。雖然《馬可福音》只有《馬太福音》的三分之二的篇幅，可是其中的大部分事件都寫到了。《馬可福音》的風格精練有力，深刻，生動而優美，常常提供了其他福音書所沒有的細節。
馬可強調耶穌為一位活動家，而馬太則把耶穌描述為一位教師。所以馬可記錄了其他同觀福音書所記載的幾乎全部的神蹟。馬可所用的 eutheos （“立即”）一詞比其他幾本福音書加起來還多（見可1：10註釋）。
馬可主要按年代敘述耶穌生平，而不是象馬太那樣按講題來敘述。他側重於神蹟，說明他想通過耶穌所行的神蹟奇事彰顯上帝的大能。這就是馬可為耶穌的神性所作的主要見證，正如馬太表現耶穌應驗了舊約先知預言的事實。馬太根據耶穌是先知所見證的一位，從而證明祂是彌賽亞。馬可則通過見證祂的神能而證明祂是彌賽亞，這對於他心目中的讀者──外邦人中的基督徒，也許是羅馬人──更有說服力一些。
0.en:
**1. Title.** The earliest extant manuscripts bear the simple title “According to Mark.” Later, as the term “gospel” came to be applied to the story of Jesus’ life and ministry, it was incorporated into the title of this book. The title found in the KJV, “The Gospel According to St. Mark,” appears only in late manuscripts.
**2. Authorship.** The unanimous and consistent testimony of Christian tradition points to John Mark as the author of the Gospel that bears his name. The name Mark is from the Latin Marcus, and is the surname of the writer (Acts 12:12, 25). His first name was John (see ch. 13:5, 13). His mother’s name was Mary (ch. 12:12). He was a cousin of Barnabas (Col. 4:10), who at one time had been a resident of the island of Cyprus (Acts 4:36). Mark’s home in Jerusalem seems to have been the house in which was the “upper room” (see on Matt. 26:18), where, for a time at least, some of the apostles lived after the resurrection and the ascension (John 20:19; Acts 1:13), and where members of the early church in Jerusalem assembled (Acts 12:12). It was John Mark who accompanied Paul and Barnabas on the first part of their first missionary journey (ch. 13:5, 13). On a later journey, Mark accompanied Barnabas to the island of Cyprus (ch. 15:36–39). Later he seems to have worked under the direction of Peter and Paul (1 Peter 5:13; Col. 4:10 2 Tim. 4:11). The fact that the Gospel carries the name of so inconspicuous a man as Mark is indirect evidence of its genuineness and of his authorship. Had the book been a forgery, the name of a more well-known person who had been associated personally with Jesus, such as the apostle Peter, would no doubt have been attached to it. There is no valid reason to doubt either the authenticity of the book or that Mark was its author. Papias, bishop of the city of Hierapolis, about 10 mi. (16 km.) from Collossae and Laodicea in Asia Minor, is the first known writer who speaks of Mark as the author of this Gospel. In his Interpretations, as quoted in Eusebius (Ecclesiastical History iii. 39. 15; Loeb ed., vol. 1, p. 297), he states:
“‘And the Presbyter [most probably the presbyter John] used to say this, “Mark became Peter’s interpreter and wrote accurately all that he remembered, not, indeed, in order, of the things said or done by the Lord. For he had not heard the Lord, nor had he followed him, but later on, as I said, followed Peter, who used to give teaching as necessity demanded but not making, as it were, an arrangement of the Lord’s oracles, so that Mark did nothing wrong in thus writing down single points as he remembered them. For to one thing he gave attention, to leave out nothing of what he had heard and to make no false statements in them.”’”
This statement is in harmony with Peter’s reference to Mark as “my son” (1 Peter 5:13).
Papias’ report is taken generally to imply that Mark served as a translator for the apostle Peter when he addressed audiences in whose language he was not fluent, apparently on journeys in lands where Aramaic, Peter’s native tongue, was not spoken. However, see AA 40. Presumably, Mark translated Peter’s gospel account so often that he became familiar with it and thus was prepared to write the gospel narrative under inspiration of the Holy spirit. Most scholars agree that Mark’s record is the earliest of the four Gospels.
The Church Fathers are not in agreement as to whether Mark wrote before or after Peter’s death (c. .. 64–66). Irenaeus of Lyons (c. .. 185) declares that Mark’s Gospel was written after Peter died (Against Heresies iii. 1. 1). Clement of Alexandria (c. .. 190), on the other hand, places the writing of Mark during the lifetime of Peter (Eusebius, op. cit., vi. 14. 5–7; Loeb ed., vol. 2, pp. 47, 49). The latter view appears to agree more closely with available information. But whichever was the case, the writing of this Gospel is doubtless to be placed between the years .. 55 and 70.
Many statements in the Gospel of Mark make evident that it was written for non-Jewish readers. Such a words as kenturiōn (Latin centurio, “centurion”; ch. 15:39) and spekoulator (Latin speculator, “executioner”; ch. 6:27) suggest that while written in Greek, the language of culture, it was intended for Romans. Mark might have used the common Greek words for these officers, rather than the Latin, but he seems repeatedly to have chosen Latin words in Greek transliteration, presumably because they would be more familiar to his readers. He explains Palestinian coinage (ch. 12:42), obviously because his intended readers were not familiar with it. Similarly, he explains the Jewish Passover (ch. 14:12) and customs of the Pharisees (ch. 7:3, 4). He translates various Aramaic words and expressions (chs. 5:41; 7:34; 15:34). None of this would have been necessary for a Palestinian reading audience. At the same time the writer was obviously a Jew who knew Aramaic and was familiar with the Old Testament, which, however, he quotes from the LXX translation.
**3. Historical Setting.** For a brief outline of the historical background of the life and mission of Jesus see p. 272. For a more complete discussion see pp. 41-67.
**4. Theme.** Mark is the shortest of the Gospels, yet in some respects it is the most vigorous and powerful of them all. Though only two thirds the length of Matthew, it contains a record of most of the incidents related in its longer counterpart. Its style is terse, vigorous, incisive, vivid, picturesque, and often provides significant details not mentioned by any of the other evangelists.
Mark emphasizes Jesus as a Man of action, whereas Matthew presents Him as a Teacher. Thus Mark records almost all the miracles that are reported by both the other synoptic writers. A characteristic word of Mark’s is eutheōs (or euthus), “straightway,” or “immediately,” which he uses more often than all the other gospel writers together. See on ch. 1:10.
Mark relates the life of Christ largely in chronological order, rather than topically as Matthew does. His emphasis on miracles makes apparent his purpose to highlight the mighty power of God as evidenced by the many “signs” and “wonders” performed by Jesus. This is Mark’s primary testimony to the divinity of Jesus, as that of Matthew is the fact that He fulfilled the predictions of the prophets of old. Matthew proves Jesus the Messiah on the basis that He is the One to whom the prophets bore witness. Mark proves Him the Messiah by the witness of His divine power, which, presumably, would be more convincing to his intended readers—Christians of a Gentile, perhaps Roman, background. See pp. 191, 272-274.
**5. Outline.** In view of the fact that a full, chronological outline of the Gospel of Mark appears on pp. 196–201, the outline presented here covers only the major phases of the life and ministry of Jesus: I. Preparation for Ministry, Autumn, .. 27, 1:1–13. II. Galilean Ministry, Passover to Passover, .. 29–30, 1:14 to 7:23. A. Early Galilean ministry, 1:14–34. B. The first missionary journey, 1:35–45. C. Ministry in and about Capernaum, 2:1 to 3:19. D. The second missionary journey, 3:20 to 5:43. E. The third missionary journey, 6:1 to 7:23. III. Retirement From Public Ministry, Spring to Autumn, .. 30, 7:24 to 9:50. A. Ministry in regions bordering on Galilee, 7:24 to 8:10. B. Looking forward to the cross, 8:11 to 9:50. IV. Peraean Ministry, Autumn to Spring, .. 30–31, 10:1–52. V. Closing Ministry at Jerusalem, Passover, .. 31, 11:1 to 15:47. A. Conflict with scribes and Pharisees, 11:1 to 12:44. B. Jesus’ prophecy of the fall of Jerusalem and of His second coming, 13:1–37. C. The arrest and trial of Jesus, 14:1 to 15:20. D. The crucifixion and burial of Jesus, 15:21–47. VI The Resurrection; Postresurrection Appearances, 16:1–20.
